TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r4.claim: All strength and honor belong to God, so Islam permits reverence for others only when it leads back to God, as in honoring the Messenger, believers, and divine signs.
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r4.anchor: فلا خضوع في الإسلام لأحد دون الله إلا ما يرجع إليه تعالى ويقصد به

TABATABAI:11:17-24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:17-24/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:11:17-24/r3.claim: Abu Ja‘far identifies Ali, rather than Ibn Salam, as the one with knowledge of the Book and connects three Qur’anic descriptions to him.
TABATABAI:11:17-24/r3.anchor: قال أبو مريم حدث علينا الحديث الذي حدثتني به عن أبي جعفر قال كنت عند أبي جعفر جالسا إذ مر علينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r10.claim: Wali is interpreted as a supporter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r10.anchor: وفسر الولي هنا بالناصر، أو المتولي الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation of wali is one who manages affairs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r11.anchor: أو المتولي الأمر، أو المحب. ثلاثة أقوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r12.claim: A third interpretation of wali is a loving friend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r12.anchor: أو المتولي الأمر، أو المحب. ثلاثة أقوال، والمعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r13.claim: The singular wali is used for multiple allies because it is a generic noun, or because God's authority is primary and the others follow; a plural would hide that priority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r13.anchor: وقال: وليكم بالإفراد، ولم يقل أولياؤكم وإن كان المخبر به متعددا، لأن وليا اسم جنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r14.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r14.claim: Abdullah's reading has 'your patron' (mawlākum) instead of 'your ally' (waliyyukum).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r15.claim: The phrase 'those who believe' is general, encompassing believers who came before and those who remain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p299#2/r15.anchor: وظاهر قوله: والذين آمنوا، عموم من آمن من مضى منهم ومن بقي قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r1.speaker: الباقر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r1.claim: Asked whether the verse was revealed about Ali, al-Baqir replies that Ali is among the believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r1.anchor: وسئل الباقر عمن نزلت فيه هذه الآية، أهو علي؟ فقال: علي من المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r2.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil also says, that 'those who believe' means Ali, with a plural used figuratively for one person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r2.anchor: وقيل: الذين آمنوا هو علي رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس، وبه قال مقاتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r3.claim: One identification is Ibn Salam and his companions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r3.anchor: وقيل ابن سلام وأصحابه. وقيل: عبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r4.claim: Another identification is Ubada, after he disavowed his Jewish allies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r4.anchor: وقيل: عبادة لما تبرأ من حلفائه اليهود. وقيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r5.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r5.claim: Ikrima identifies the believers as Abu Bakr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r5.anchor: وقيل: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه، قاله عكرمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r6.claim: The prayer and almsgiving traits distinguish sincere believers from hypocrites, who do not persist in prayer or charity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r6.anchor: هذه أوصاف ميز بها المؤمن الخالص الإيمان من المنافق، لأن المنافق لا يدوم على الصلاة ولا على الزكاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r7.claim: The companions were established in prayer and almsgiving when the verse was revealed, and both acts showed humility before God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r7.anchor: ولما كانت الصحابة وقت نزول هذه الآية من مقيمي صلاة ومؤتي زكاة، وفي كلتا الحالتين كانوا متصفين بالخضوع لله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r8.claim: Ruku' most naturally means submission or humility, rather than the physical bowing posture.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r8.anchor: والركوع هنا ظاهره الخضوع، لا الهيئة التي في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r9.claim: Another view takes ruku' literally as the prayer bow, a major pillar standing for the whole prayer; the repeated prayer reference may emphasize its importance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r9.anchor: وقيل: المراد الهيئة، وخصت بالذكر لأنها من أعظم أركان الصلاة، فعبر بها عن جميع الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r10.claim: A further view takes prayer as obligatory prayers and ruku' as voluntary prayer, since 'he bows' can mean that he performs voluntary prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالصلاة هنا الفرائض، وبالركوع التنفل. يقال: فلان يركع إذا تنفل بالصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r11.claim: A report says Ali gave his ring as alms while bowing in prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r11.anchor: وروي أن عليا رضي الله عنه تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r12.claim: The phrase “while they bow” is apparently a nominal clause coordinated with the previous descriptions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r12.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: وهم راكعون، أنها جملة اسمية معطوفة على الجمل قبلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r13.claim: An alternative takes the waw as circumstantial: they give alms humbly without condescension toward recipients, while engaged in prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r13.anchor: وقيل: الواو للحال أي: يؤتون الزكاة وهم خاضعون لا يشتغلون على من يعطونهم إياها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r14.claim: Zamakhshari parses 'those who establish prayer' as an appositive of 'those who believe' or as the predicate of an omitted 'they are'; Abū Ḥayyān argues that an adjectival reading is more natural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p300/r14.anchor: الرفع على البدل من الذين آمنوا، أو على هم الذين يقيمون انتهى. ولا أدري ما الذي منعه من الصفة إذ هو المتبادر إلى الذهن

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.claim: Verses 5:51–57 set political boundaries by warning Muslims against taking Jews and Christians as protectors to the exclusion of their own religious community.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r31.anchor: in vv. 51–57, political boundaries are established between these communities, as Muslims are warned not to take Jews and Christians as protectors to the exclusion of members of the Muslim religious community

STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.claim: Islamic Law allows treaties of alliance between Muslim states and Christian or Jewish political entities.
STUDYQURAN:5:intro/r32.anchor: Islamic Law does allow treaties of alliance between the Muslim state, or states, and Christian or Jewish political entities).

THALABI:v4p80/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p80/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، عتبة بن حكيم، ثابت بن عبد الله
THALABI:v4p80/r1.claim: They identify the believers described as establishing prayer and giving alms while bowing with Ali, who gave his ring to a petitioner while bowing in the mosque.
THALABI:v4p80/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقال السدي، وعتبة بن حكيم، وثابت بن عبد الله: إنما يعني بقوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة الآية. علي بن أبي طالب

THALABI:v4p80/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p80/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v4p80/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet praising Ali as the leader of the righteous and describing how Ali gave his ring to a petitioner while bowing; the Prophet prayed for Ali as his minister and support, invoking Moses' prayer and God's promise to strengthen Moses through Aaron.
THALABI:v4p80/r2.anchor: فأنا جندب بن جنادة البدري، أبو ذر الغفاري: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بهاتين وإلا صمتا ورأيته بهاتين وإلا فعميتا يقول: علي قائد البررة

THALABI:v4p81/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v4p81/r1.claim: Abu Dharr continues the report: before the Prophet finished his prayer, Gabriel came with the command to recite the verse identifying God, the Messenger, and the believers as guardians.
THALABI:v4p81/r1.anchor: قال أبو ذر: فو الله ما استتم رسول الله الكلمة حتى أنزل عليه جبرئيل من عند الله، فقال: يا محمد اقرأ

THALABI:v4p81/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
THALABI:v4p81/r2.claim: Ahmad says no Companion has received as many reports of merits as Ali ibn Abi Talib.
THALABI:v4p81/r2.anchor: سمعت أحمد بن حنبل يقول: ما جاء لأحد من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الفضائل مثل ما جاء لعلي بن أبي طالب

THALABI:v4p81/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p81/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the verse identifying the believers as guardians was revealed concerning Abu Bakr.
THALABI:v4p81/r3.anchor: عن سفيان عن أبيه عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت في أبي بكر إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الآيتان الخبر

THALABI:v4p81/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p81/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v4p81/r4.claim: He interprets the believers as protectors of one another and says whoever takes God, the Messenger, and the believers as allies belongs to God's victorious party.
THALABI:v4p81/r4.anchor: قال: سألت أبا جعفر عن قوله إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا قال: هم المؤمنون بعضهم أولياء بعض

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r1.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r1.claim: The verse continues the protector discussion from 5:51 and reiterates that believers should take only God, His Messenger, and believers as protectors.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r1.anchor: This verse continues the discussion of protectors begun in v. 51, reiterating that the believers should take only God

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r2.claim: God is the primary walī and Walī is one of His Names; taking the Prophet and believers as protectors follows naturally from one's relation of walāyah to God.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r2.anchor: one of whose Names is Walī, and one then takes His Prophet and the other believers as awliyāʾ

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r3.claim: Some see an endorsement of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, who left alliance with Jewish clans and pledged allegiance solely to the Prophet and his community.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r3.anchor: Some consider this verse to be an endorsement of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r4.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r4.claim: Others read it as a response to Companions socially ostracized by Banū Qurayẓah and Banū Naḍīr.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r4.anchor: Others consider it to be a response to some Companions of the Prophet who complained about being socially ostracized

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r5.claim: Those praying and giving alms while bowing may refer to believers generally or sincere believers free from hypocrisy.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r5.anchor: can be understood as a description of the believers in general (Ṭ) or of the sincere believers who are untainted by hypocrisy

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r6.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r6.claim: Bowing while praying and giving alms may indicate performing these religious deeds humbly.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r6.anchor: may also indicate that one performs these religious deeds in a state of humility

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r7.speaker: early authorities
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r7.claim: Many early authorities, including Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, specifically identify ʿAlī; reports describe him giving his ring to a person asking charity while he bowed in prayer.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r7.anchor: including the influential early commentators Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, considered this to be a specific reference to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r8.claim: The ʿAlī account encourages giving charity when requested and emulating his virtue in not delaying help until prayer ends.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r8.anchor: encouraging the practice of giving charity whenever it is requested and recommending that believers seek to emulate Alī’s high degree of virtue

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r9.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r9.claim: A minority tradition identifies Abū Bakr as the referent.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r9.anchor: A minority tradition considers this verse to be a reference to Abū Bakr

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r10.claim: Shiites call it the verse of wilāyah/walāyah; beyond protector or friend, these terms name a spiritual authority especially important in Shiism.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r10.anchor: Shiites sometimes refer to this verse as the “verse of wilāyah/walāyah.”

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r11.speaker: Shiites
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r11.claim: Shiites read the verse as identifying ʿAlī as walī after God and the Prophet, affirming his unique spiritual authority and right to succeed the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r11.anchor: Shiites, who have used these terms traditionally to refer to the unique spiritual authority of ʿAlī

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r12.speaker: Sunni authors
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r12.claim: Some Sunni authors accept the early association with ʿAlī but say its traditions are unsound or do not establish Shiite legitimist conclusions.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r12.anchor: A number of Sunni authors who acknowledge the widespread connection of this verse to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r13.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects spiritual authority as the meaning of wilāyah here, taking it as friendship or mutual support.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r13.anchor: Al-Rāzī, for example, denies that wilāyah/walāyah means anything other than friendship or mutual support here

STUDYQURAN:5:55/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r14.claim: Despite Sunni objections to its legitimist reading, the widespread association with ʿAlī among Sunni commentaries and early authorities supports its authenticity in early tafsīr tradition.
STUDYQURAN:5:55/r14.anchor: the prevalence of the association of this verse with ʿAlī, even in Sunni commentaries and among some of the earliest authorities

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r1.claim: The believers have no protector or helper except God, His Messenger, and the believers characterized by the verse.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r1.anchor: وقال: أتولى الله ورسوله والمؤمنين، وأبرأ من حلف الكفار وولايتهم

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r2.claim: The Jews and Christians whom God ordered Muslims to disavow are not their allies or helpers; rather, they ally with one another.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r2.anchor: فأما اليهود والنصارى الذين أمركم الله أن تبرءوا من ولايتهم ونهاكم أن تتخذوا منهم أولياء، فليسوا لكم أولياء ولا نصراء، بل بعضهم أولياء بعض

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.speaker: عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed when ʿUbādah renounced his alliance with Banū Qaynuqāʿ after their war with Muhammad and declared allegiance to God, the Messenger, and the believers.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r3.anchor: عن عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت، قال: لما حاربت بنو قينقاع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، مشى عبادة بن الصامت إلى رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r4.speaker: عطية بن سعد
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r4.claim: A report from ʿAṭiyya ibn Saʿd gives a similar account of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit coming to the Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r4.anchor: عن عطية بن سعد، قال: جاء عبادة بن الصامت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثم ذكر نحوه

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that whoever accepts Islam comes under the protection of God and His Messenger.

TAB-FULL:v8p529/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r6.claim: Al-Suddī takes the referent to be all believers, while explaining that ʿAlī once gave his ring to a supplicant while bowing in the mosque.
TAB-FULL:v8p529/r6.anchor: عن السدي، قال: ثم أخبرهم بمن، يتولاهم

TAB-FULL:v8p531/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says the phrase means believers generally; when told it was reportedly revealed about ʿAlī, he replies that ʿAlī is among the believers.
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r1.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، قال: سألته عن هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v8p531/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r2.speaker: عتبة بن أبي حكيم
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r2.claim: ʿUtba ibn Ḥakīm identifies the believers in this verse as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r2.anchor: قال: ثنا عتبة بن أبي حكيم

TAB-FULL:v8p531/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p531/r3.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who gave charity while bowing.

TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.claim: Some exegetes treat these verses as continuous with the bans on alliance and read wilaya as support, restricted to God, the Messenger, and true believers; they connect them to 3:68, 33:6, 8:72, and 9:71.
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r1.anchor: جماعة من مفسري القوم إشتراكهما مع ما قبلهما وما بعدهما

TABATABAI:5:55-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r2.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r2.claim: On that reading, the specified believers are the true faithful, excluding hypocrites and the sick at heart, and the verse assigns them mutual support with God and the Messenger.
TABATABAI:5:55-56/r2.anchor: وهؤلاء هم المؤمنون حقا فيخرج بذلك المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r1.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r1.claim: To explain while bowing in the support reading, some interpreters take bowing figuratively as humility before God or as a condition of poverty and need when giving alms.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r1.anchor: بحمل الركوع على معناه المجازي وهو مطلق الخضوع لله سبحانه أو انحطاط الحال لفقر ونحوه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects a unified context: although the surah was revealed late, its verses came down at different times, as their content and occasions of revelation show; adjacency does not prove common occasion or context.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r2.anchor: فليس مجرد وقوع الآية بعد الآية أو قبل الآية يدل على وحدة السياق

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r3.claim: The preceding passage forbids believers' alliance with Jews and Christians and criticizes hypocrites for seeking their favor without addressing those communities; the following passage directly addresses the forbidden groups, so their purposes differ.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r3.anchor: فالغرض في القبيلين من الآيات السابقة واللاحقة مختلف، ومعه كيف يتحد السياق

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r4.claim: The prior passage's clauses that each group are one another's allies and that an ally becomes one of them do not fit a mere support pact; they describe affectionate alliance and spiritual-social assimilation.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r4.anchor: بخلاف عقد ولاية المودة التي توجب الامتزاج النفسي والروحي بين الطرفين

TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.claim: The alternative reading of bowing makes the verse say that believers' guardians are God, the Messenger, and faithful worshippers who submit to God's lordship in obedience, or give alms while poor.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#2/r5.anchor: ويعود معنى الآية إلى أنه ليس أولياؤكم اليهود والنصارى والمنافقين بل أولياؤكم الله ورسوله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.claim: It is improper to call the Prophet a supporter of believers in the relevant religious sense; support is rendered to God's religion, which God legislates and the Messenger and believers uphold.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r1.anchor: على أنه ليس من الجائز أن يعد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وليا للمؤمنين بمعنى ولاية النصرة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r2.claim: The Qur'an calls the disciples helpers of God and describes support for God's cause and covenant with prophets to believe in and support the coming messenger.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r3.claim: The Qur'an also praises the Prophet's supporters, those who aid God's Messenger, and the Helpers who sheltered and supported the emigrants.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r4.claim: Since believers are bound to God's religious law, the Qur'an describes God as supporting those who support Him and as supporting His messengers and believers.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.claim: Religion cannot belong only to believers with the Prophet outside it and then make him their supporter: he shares every religious distinction in its fullest measure, and the Qur'an never calls him their supporter.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#3/r5.anchor: ولا في آية واحدة، وحاشا ساحة الكلام الإلهي أن يساهل

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r1.claim: Qur’anic wilāya ascribed to the Prophet means authority to direct affairs or love and affection, not the community’s need to support him.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r1.anchor: أن المراد بما نسب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الولاية في القرآن هو ولاية التصرف أو الحب والمودة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.claim: The promise of victory fits authority, love, and support alike; religious victory comes through connection to God and His Messenger by any means.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r2.anchor: فإن الغلبة كما تناسب الولاية بمعنى النصرة، كذلك تناسب ولاية التصرف وكذا ولاية المحبة والمودة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.claim: Numerous Shia and Sunni reports say both verses were revealed about Ali when he gave his ring during prayer.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r3.anchor: على أن الروايات متكاثرة من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة على أن الآيتين نازلتان في أمير المؤمنين علي عليه السلام لما تصدق بخاتمه وهو في الصلاة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.claim: Rejecting abundant transmitted occasions of revelation would make transmitted occasions for any Qur’anic verse unreliable.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r4.anchor: لم يصح الركون إلى شيء من أسباب النزول المأثورة في شيء من آيات القرآن

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r5.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r5.claim: Objectors say the surrounding context concerns mutual support, so these verses should mean support as well.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r5.anchor: استشكلوا في الروايات - ولم يكن ينبغي أن يستشكل فيها

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r6.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r6.claim: Objectors argue that the plural believers must mean one person, Ali, which Arabic does not permit.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r6.anchor: على هذا التقدير هو علي ولا يساعده اللغة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r7.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r7.claim: Objectors argue that giving a ring cannot be called zakāt.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r7.anchor: وثالثا أن لازمها كون المراد بالزكاة هو التصدق بالخاتم، ولا يسمى ذلك زكاة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r8.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r8.claim: They therefore prefer a general reading, framed as restrictive correction or specification, opposing hypocrites’ allegiance to the People of the Book.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#4/r8.anchor: قالوا فالمتعين أن تؤخذ الآية عامة، وتكون مسوقة لمثل قصر القلب أو الإفراد فقد كان المنافقون يسارعون إلى ولاية أهل الكتاب

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r1.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r1.claim: To preserve a general reading, objectors take bowing metaphorically as humility, poverty, or a shabby condition.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r1.anchor: ولا يبقى إلا مخالفة هذا المعنى لظاهر قوله { وهم راكعون } ويندفع بحمل الركوع على معناه المجازي، وهو الخضوع لله أو الفقر ورثاثة الحال

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.claim: Close reading rejects all objections: these verses do not serve the prior context’s support theme, even if earlier verses did.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r2.anchor: لكن التدبر في الآية وما يناظرها من الآيات يوجب سقوط الوجوه المذكورة جميعا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r3.claim: Arabic distinguishes using a plural form for one person from stating a collective rule or description whose only valid instance may be one person; the latter is common.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r3.anchor: وأنّه فرق بين إطلاق لفظ الجمع وإرادة الواحد واستعماله فيه، وبين إعطاء حكم كلي أو الإخبار بمعرف جمعي

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r4.claim: Reported single-person occasions illustrate plural wording: Hatib b. Abi Baltaʿa, ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy, one questioner, and a spender identified as Ali or Abu Bakr.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r4.anchor: وقد صح أن المراد به حاطب بن أبي بلتعة في مكاتبته قريشا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r5.claim: The nearby phrase about fearing a reversal is attributed to ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy, and the verse is within this same passage.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r5.anchor: والقائل هو عبد الله بن أبي، على ما رووا في سبب نزوله وتلقوه بالقبول

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r6.claim: Even if plurals include like-minded followers, that proves Arabic permits collective usage; here it signals that religious honors, including wilāya, follow sincerity and deeds.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r6.anchor: قيل إن محصله جواز ذلك في اللغة لنكتة مجوزة فليجر الآية أعني قوله { والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون }

TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r7.claim: Most transmitters were Companions and Successors fluent in native Arabic; their acceptance without objection supports the legitimacy of collective plural usage.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#5/r7.anchor: ولو كان هذا النحو من الاستعمال لا تبيحه اللغة ولا يعهده أهلها

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r1.claim: The technical legal sense of zakāt arose after Qur’anic revelation; linguistically the word is broader and can mean spending wealth for God, especially alongside prayer.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r1.anchor: إنما تحقق في عرف المتشرعة بعد نزول القرآن بوجوبها وتشريعها في الدين، وأما الذي تعطيه اللغة فهو أعم من الزكاة المصطلحة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r2.claim: Earlier prophets are described as giving zakāt despite lacking the later Islamic financial obligation, showing the word’s broader use.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r2.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن ليس في شرائعهم الزكاة المالية بالمعنى الذي اصطلح عليه في الإسلام

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r3.claim: Meccan passages use zakāt before its technical institution, including early revelations; their intended meaning cannot be the later legal obligation.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r3.anchor: ولم تكن شرعت الزكاة المصطلحة بعد فليت شعري ماذا كان يفهمه المسلمون من هذه الآيات في لفظ الزكاة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r4.claim: Qur’an 9:103 makes zakāt a kind of charity, named for charity’s general purifying effect; usage later became dominant for obligatory charity.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r4.anchor: أن الزكاة من أفراد الصدقة، وإنما سميت زكاة لكون الصدقة مطهرة مزكية مطلقا، وقد غلب استعمالها في الصدقة المصطلحة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r5.claim: Any charity or spending for God may be called zakāt, so neither metaphorical bowing nor a special grammatical workaround for singular wali with plural believers is needed.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r5.anchor: أنه لا مانع من تسمية مطلق الصدقة والإنفاق في سبيل الله زكاة، وتبين أيضا أن لا موجب لارتكاب خلاف الظاهر بحمل الركوع على معناه المجازي

TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r6.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib defines walāʾ and tawālī as close succession, extended from spatial proximity to relations such as kinship, friendship, support, and belief; wilāya can mean support or taking charge.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#6/r6.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الولاء بفتح الواو والتوالي أن يحصل شيئان فصاعدا حصولا ليس بينهما ما ليس منهما

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib says tawallā with a direct object denotes turning toward it; with ʿan, expressed or understood, it denotes turning away.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r1.anchor: وقولهم تولى إذا عدي بنفسه اقتضى معنى الولاية وحصوله في أقرب المواضع منه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r2.claim: The concept of wilāya began with physical and temporal closeness, then extended to abstract relations because people first engage with sensible things.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن القرب الكذائي المعبر عنه بالولاية، أول ما اعتبره الإنسان إنما اعتبره في الأجسام وأمكنتها وأزمنتها ثم استعير لأقسام القرب المعنوية

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r3.claim: Abstract wilāya is a special closeness that grants a right to manage another’s affairs: examples include heirs, guardians, supporters, God, prophets, rulers, and other forms of authority or bond.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r3.anchor: المحصل من معنى الولاية في موارد استعمالها هو نحو من القرب يوجب نوعا من حق التصرف ومالكية التدبير

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r4.claim: The phrases about turning backs and turning away mean facing the battle’s opposite direction or directing oneself away from the intended course.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r4.anchor: وقوله { يولون الأدبار } أي يجعلون أدبارهم تلي جهة الحرب وتدبر أمرها، وقوله { توليتم } أي توليتم عن قبوله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.claim: The coordinated list under one singular wali indicates one sense of wilāya for God, the Messenger, and believers; the next verse likewise treats them together as God’s party.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#7/r5.anchor: على ما يدل على وحدة ما في معنى الولاية المذكورة فيه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r1.claim: God’s ontological wilāya permits Him to act in anything and manage creation as He wills; Qur’anic parallels describe Him as the sole guardian and one nearer than the jugular vein.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r1.anchor: الولاية التكوينية التي تصحح له التصرف في كل شيء وتدبير أمر الخلق بما شاء وكيف شاء

TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r2.claim: God’s supporting wilāya may belong to this domain; Qur’an says He is the believers’ patron and helper, while unbelievers have no patron.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r2.anchor: وربما لحق بهذا الباب ولاية النصرة التي ذكرها لنفسه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r3.claim: God also has wilāya over believers’ religious affairs through legislation, guidance, direction, and enabling.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r3.anchor: وذكر تعالى أيضا لنفسه الولاية على المؤمنين فيما يرجع إلى أمر دينهم من تشريع الشريعة والهداية والإرشاد والتوفيق

TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r4.claim: God’s wilāya in the Qur’an reduces to ontological and legislative authority, also describable as real and conventional wilāya.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r4.anchor: ويرجع محصلها إلى ولاية التكوين وولاية التشريع، وإن شئت سميتهما بالولاية الحقيقية والولاية الاعتبارية

TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r5.claim: The Prophet’s distinctive wilāya is legislative: he conveys law, calls and educates the community, governs it, and judges its affairs.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#8/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر الله سبحانه لنبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الولاية التي تخصه الولاية التشريعية وهي القيام بالتشريع والدعوة وتربية الأمة والحكم فيهم والقضاء في أمرهم

TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r1.claim: The Prophet’s legislative authority includes guiding people to God, teaching scripture, clarifying revelation, commanding obedience, and judging by what God revealed; God does not assign him support-wilāya over the community.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r1.anchor: ويجمع الجميع أن له صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الولاية على الأمة في سوقهم إلى الله والحكم فيهم والقضاء عليهم في جميع شؤونهم

TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r2.claim: The Prophet’s authority entails absolute obedience and is God’s legislative wilāya delegated to him, since obedience to the Messenger is obedience to God.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r2.anchor: فله عليهم الإطاعة المطلقة فترجع ولايته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى ولاية الله سبحانه بالولاية التشريعية

TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r3.claim: The wilāya shared by God, the Messenger, and believers is one kind: original in God and granted derivatively to the others by His permission.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r3.anchor: على ما عرفت من دلالة السياق على كون هذه الولاية ولاية واحدة هي لله سبحانه بالاصالة ولرسوله والذين آمنوا بالتبع وبإذن منه تعالى

TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r4.claim: If God’s and believers’ wilāya meant different things, the verse would distinguish them as Qur’an does by repeating īmān when it has different senses.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#9/r4.anchor: ولو كانت الولاية المنسوبة إلى الله تعالى في الآية غير المنسوبة إلى الذين آمنوا - والمقام مقام الالتباس

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r1.claim: The restriction in innamā is best read as qasr al-ifrād: it singles out the named guardians against people who thought others also held wilāya; qasr al-qalb is also possible.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r1.anchor: أن القصر في قوله { إنما وليكم الله } " الخ " ، لقصر الإفراد

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r2.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r2.claim: Exegetes explain singular wali with plural believers as one wilāya, original for God and derivative for the others.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r2.anchor: وقد وجهه المفسرون بكون الولاية ذات معنى واحد هو لله سبحانه على الاصالة ولغيره بالتبع

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r3.claim: The phrase about establishing prayer, giving zakāt, and bowing identifies the believers mentioned immediately before it.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r4.claim: The clause wa-hum rākiʿūn is circumstantial and modifies the subject of yuʾtūn; yuʾtūn is its governing word.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r4.anchor: وقوله { وهم راكعون } حال من فاعل { يؤتون } وهو العامل فيه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r5.claim: Rukūʿ names the familiar human posture and, in religious usage, the posture in worship; it symbolizes humility and is prescribed in Islam only within prayer, unlike prostration.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r5.anchor: والركوع هو الهيئة المخصوصة في الإنسان، ومنه الشيخ الراكع، ويطلق في عرف الشرع على الهيئة المخصوصة في العبادة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r6.claim: Because bowing embodies humility, it can figuratively mean general abasement or poverty and hardship, usually accompanied by subordination.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#10/r6.anchor: ولكونه مشتملا على الخضوع والتذلل ربما استعير لمطلق التذلل والخضوع أو الفقر والإعسار

TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r4.claim: In al-Kāfī, Imam al-Bāqir says God commanded the Prophet to proclaim Ali’s wilāya; after fearing rejection, the Prophet proclaimed it at Ghadir Khumm, and wilāya was the final obligation completing religion.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#11/r4.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال أمر الله عز وجل رسوله بولاية علي وأنزل عليه { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r2.claim: Al-Qummī reports from Imam al-Bāqir that the verse descended while the Prophet sat with Jewish converts including ʿAbd Allah b. Salām; he then found the petitioner, and it was Ali; al-ʿAyyāshī also transmits it.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم جالس وعنده قوم من اليهود فيهم عبد الله بن سلام إذ نزلت عليه هذه الآية

TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r3.claim: In al-Amālī, Abu Rafi recounts protecting the sleeping Prophet from a snake; the Prophet awakes reciting 5:55, praises Ali, predicts a rightful fight against Ali’s opponents, calls that fight jihad, and prays for Abu Rafi’s strength.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#12/r3.anchor: عن جده أبي رافع قال دخلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يوما وهو نائم وحية في جانب البيت فكرهت أن أقتلها وأوقظ النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r1.claim: Abu Rafi recalls the Prophet calling him his trusted one; after Ali's accession he sold his property and followed Ali through Basra, Ṣiffīn, and Nahrawān.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r1.anchor: إن لكل نبي أمينا، وإن أميني أبو رافع

TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r2.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r2.claim: Ammar reports that Ali gave a ring to a petitioner while bowing in a voluntary prayer; the verse descended, and the Prophet proclaimed Ali his mawla.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r2.anchor: سمعت عمار بن ياسر يقول وقف لعلي بن أبي طالب سائل وهو راكع في صلاة تطوع

TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r3.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r3.claim: One of the two Imams reports that the revelation of this verse distressed the Prophet, who feared Quraysh would deny him; God then commanded him in 5:67 to proclaim it at Ghadir Khumm.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r3.anchor: عن المفضل بن صالح، عن بعض أصحابه، عن أحدهما عليهما السلام

TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r4.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r4.claim: One of the two Imams reports that God instructed the Prophet to love Ali, Abu Dharr, Salman, and Miqdad; only three people knew the matter of authority.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#13/r4.anchor: عن أبي جميلة عن بعض أصحابه عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r1.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r1.claim: The report concludes that people who came to the knowledgeable authorities did not ask whom the verses on authority referred to.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r1.anchor: من ثم أتاهم لم يكونوا يسألون

TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r2.claim: In his appeal to Abu Bakr, Ali asks whether God's authority joined to the Messenger's in the ring-alms verse belonged to him or Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr answers that it belonged to Ali.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r2.anchor: في حديث مناشدة علي عليه السلام لأبي بكر حين ولي أبو بكر الخلافة، وذكر عليه السلام فضائله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r3.claim: Abu Dharr reports Ali's challenge at the shura: no one else gave alms while bowing and had this verse revealed about him; the other candidates agreed.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r3.anchor: إلى أبي ذر في حديث مناشدة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام عثمان والزبير وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص

TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r4.speaker: علي بن محمد الهادي
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r4.claim: Al-Hadi's letter treats the Qur'an and the community's agreement on its truth as decisive evidence, interpreting the hadith about communal consensus as excluding fabricated reports and readings that overturn clear scripture.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#14/r4.anchor: علي بن محمد الهادي عليه السلام إلى أهل الأهواز حين سألوه عن الجبر والتفويض. قال عليه السلام اجتمعت الأمة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r1.claim: The author cites the Thaqalayn reports that the Qur'an and the Prophet's family will not part, and says verse 5:55 is a scriptural witness to that hadith.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r1.anchor: وجدنا شواهد هذا الحديث نصا في كتاب الله مثل قوله { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r2.claim: The author says scholars' reports agree that Ali gave his ring while bowing, for which God praised him and revealed the verse.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r2.anchor: ثم اتفقت روايات العلماء في ذلك لأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنه تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع

TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r3.claim: The author adduces the Prophet's declarations naming Ali as mawla, successor who settles debts and fulfills promises, and deputy like Aaron to Moses except for prophethood.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#15/r3.anchor: قد أبانه من أصحابه بهذه اللفظة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r1.claim: Because the Qur'an confirms these reports and they in turn clarify the Qur'an, the author says the community must acknowledge them; only obstinacy and corruption lead to refusal.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r1.anchor: فعلمنا أن الكتاب شهد بتصديق هذه الأخبار، وتحقيق هذه الشواهد

TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r2.claim: Ali reports that hypocrites asked whether any further duty remained; God identified wilayah as the single admonition in 34:46 and revealed 5:55, with only one man giving alms while bowing.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r2.anchor: وفي الاحتجاج في حديث عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام قال المنافقون لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هل بقي لربك علينا

TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r3.claim: Al-Sadiq answers that obedience to the successors is obligatory and identifies them as those described in 4:59 and 5:55.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r3.anchor: قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام الأوصياء طاعتهم مفترضة؟ فقال نعم، هم الذين قال الله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r4.claim: The author explains that attributing revelation about Ali to all the Imams reflects their single household and unified affair.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#16/r4.anchor: وإسناد نزول ما نزل في علي عليه السلام إلى جميع الأئمة عليهم السلام لكونهم أهل بيت واحد، وأمرهم واحد.

TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r1.claim: Abu Dharr recounts Ali giving a ring to a petitioner while bowing, then the Prophet praying that Ali be his minister as Aaron was to Moses; Gabriel brought 5:55 in response, and Abu Dharr calls Ali leader of the righteous and slayer of unbelievers.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r1.anchor: فكشف العمامة عن وجهه وقال يا أيها الناس من عرفني فقد عرفني ومن لم يعرفني فأنا جندب بن جنادة البدري أبو ذر الغفاري

TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.speaker: ابن سلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.claim: Ibn Salam reports that converts ostracized by their people witnessed Ali give his ring while bowing; the Prophet recited both verses after learning of the gift.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#17/r2.anchor: من صحيح النسائي عن ابن سلام قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلنا إن قومنا حادونا لما صدقنا الله ورسوله

TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r1.claim: Mujahid reports from Ibn Abbas that 5:55 was revealed about Ali.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r1.anchor: أخبرنا مجاهد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ali gave his ring to a poor man while bowing, after which the Prophet asked who had given it and the verse descended.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس قال كان علي راكعا فجاءه مسكين

TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r3.claim: Al-Baqir identifies Ali, rather than Ibn Salam, as the one possessing knowledge of the Book and as the witness in 13:43 and 11:17; he says verses including 5:55 were revealed about Ali.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r3.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، قال كنت عند أبي جعفر جالسا إذ مر عليه ابن عبد الله بن سلام

TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r4.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r4.claim: Amr tells Muawiya that several verses of distinctive merit were revealed for Ali, including 5:55, alongside verses about vows, the witness, fidelity, and affection for kin.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r4.anchor: في جواب مكاتبة معاوية إلى عمرو بن العاص قال عمرو بن العاص لقد علمت يا معاوية ما أنزل في كتابه من الآيات

TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ibn Salam and fellow converts complained that their community shunned them and the Prophet answered by reciting 5:55.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#18/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه

TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, the petitioner identifies Ali as the ring-giver and says he gave it while bowing; the Prophet then recites 5:56, completing the response to Ibn Salam's group's complaint.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r1.anchor: خرج إلى المسجد والناس بين قائم وراكع، وبصر بسائل

TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r2.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r2.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's poem praises Ali for giving his blessed ring while bowing and says God revealed the best authority for him in definitive ordinances.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r2.anchor: فأنشأ حسان بن ثابت يقول أبا حسن تفديك نفسي ومهجتي وكل بطيء في الهدى ومسارع

TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r3.claim: Anas reports that Ali gestured for a petitioner to take his ring while he bowed; the Prophet told Umar Paradise was assured for Ali, who thereby shed every sin and error.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r3.anchor: أن سائلا أتى المسجد وهو يقول من يقرض الملي الوفي؟ وعلي راكع يقول بيده خلفه للسائل

TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r4.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r4.claim: Ammar reports that Ali gave a ring to a petitioner during a voluntary prayer, prompting the verse's revelation and the Prophet's declaration that Ali was his mawla.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#19/r4.anchor: عن أبيه، عن جده قال سمعت عمار بن ياسر - رضي الله عنه - يقول وقف لعلي بن أبي طالب

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r1.speaker: جابر
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r1.claim: Jabir reports that Ibn Salam and companions complained of social isolation; a petitioner then said Ali gave him a ring while bowing, and the verse was revealed.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r1.anchor: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال جاء عبد الله بن سلام

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r2.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r2.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl reports that Ali gave his ring while bowing and the verse descended.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r2.anchor: عن موسى بن قيس الحضرمي عن سلمة بن كهيل قال تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع فنزلت

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r3.claim: Abu Rafi says the Prophet recited the verse while waking from revelation; he later foretold that people would fight Ali and prescribed resistance by hand, tongue, or heart according to ability.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r3.anchor: يا أبا رافع سيكون بعدي قوم يقاتلون عليا حق على الله جهادهم

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.claim: The author says reports of the ring-giving occasion are numerous and available in their cited books; he selected several accounts because their wording of the episode varies.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r4.anchor: أقول والروايات في نزول الآيتين في قصة التصدق بالخاتم كثيرة أخرجنا عدة منها من كتاب غاية المرام للبحراني

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.claim: The author says Companions and Imams widely transmitted the episode, and major tafsir and hadith authorities including Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Tabari, and al-Tabarani accepted it without refutation; theologians also acknowledged its report.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r5.anchor: وقد اتفق على نقلها من غير رد أئمة التفسير المأثور كأحمد والنسائي والطبري والطبراني وعبد بن حميد

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r6.claim: Jurists cite the report when discussing extensive movement during prayer and whether voluntary almsgiving counts as zakat.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r6.anchor: وأوردها الفقهاء في مسألة الفعل الكثير من بحث الصلاة، وفي مسألة

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r7.claim: Leading literary commentators such as al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan did not question that the verse applies to the ring-giving report, nor did language authorities challenge the report's wording.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r7.anchor: ولم يناقش في صحة انطباق الآية على الرواية فحول الأدب من المفسرين كالزمخشري في الكشاف

TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r8.claim: The author rejects claims that the ring report was fabricated, especially Ibn Taymiyya's assertion of scholarly consensus that it was forged, calling that claim extraordinary.
TABATABAI:5:55-56#20/r8.anchor: فلا يعبأ بما ذكره بعضهم أن حديث نزول الآية في قصة الخاتم موضوع مختلق، وقد أفرط بعضهم كشيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية

TABRISI:5:55-56/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56/r1.claim: Walī can mean the one who provides support and aid, or the one who manages an affair; examples include a woman's marriage guardian, claimant to blood retaliation, ruler, and designated heir.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r1.anchor: الولي هو الذي يلي النصرة والمعونة والولي هو الذي يلي تدبير الأمر

TABRISI:5:55-56/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r2.speaker: الكميت
TABRISI:5:55-56/r2.claim: Al-Kumayt's praise of ʿAlī uses walī al-amr for the successor who takes charge after his predecessor.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r2.anchor: الكميت يمدح عليا: ونعم ولي الأمر بعد وليه

TABRISI:5:55-56/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r3.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:5:55-56/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the root sense of walī is awlā, more entitled; mawlā has the same sense.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r3.anchor: المبرد في كتاب العبارة عن صفات الله: أصل الولي

TABRISI:5:55-56/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56/r4.claim: Rukūʿ is a particular bending or bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r4.anchor: والركوع هو التطأطؤ المخصوص. قال الخليل

TABRISI:5:55-56/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r5.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:5:55-56/r5.claim: Al-Khalīl says anything that bends forward is rukūʿ whether or not its knees touch the ground; Labīd's cited line uses rākiʿ for the bent posture.

TABRISI:5:55-56/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r6.speaker: ابن دريد
TABRISI:5:55-56/r6.claim: Ibn Durayd defines a rākiʿ as one who falls on his face, from which the prayer term is derived.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r6.anchor: ابن دريد الراكع الذي يكبو على وجهه

TABRISI:5:55-56/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r7.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:5:55-56/r7.claim: An anonymous poem uses the form تركع for the face-falling sense of the verb, illustrating Ibn Durayd's explanation.

TABRISI:5:55-56/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56/r8.claim: A humble person may be called rākiʿ figuratively because of lowered posture, as in the poem warning not to humiliate the poor.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r8.anchor: وقد يوصف الخاضع بأنه راكع على سبيل التشبيه والمجاز

TABRISI:5:55-56/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56/r10.claim: Innamā restricts what follows and denies what is not specified; the dirham and Ḥātim examples explain the rule, and al-Aʿshā's line says honor belongs to the greater party.
TABRISI:5:55-56/r10.anchor: لفظة إنما مخصصة لما أثبت بعده نافية لما لم يثبت

TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r1.claim: The continuation explains al-Aʿshā's example: the line denies honor to those who are not the greater party.
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r1.anchor: أراد نفي العزة عمن ليس بكاثر

TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r2.claim: Wa-hum rākiʿūn is an accusative circumstantial clause modifying yuʾtūna: they give zakāt while bowing, like a generous person giving wealth while smiling.
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r2.anchor: جملة في موضع النصب على الحال من يؤتون

TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r4.claim: Abū Dharr says the Prophet declared ʿAlī leader of the righteous and vanquisher of unbelievers, aided if supported and forsaken if opposed. During noon prayer a beggar received ʿAlī's ring as he signaled with his ring-bearing little finger while bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r4.anchor: فأنا بنفسي أنا جندب بن جنادة البدري أبو ذر الغفاري

TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r5.claim: In Abū Dharr's account the Prophet saw the beggar take the ring and raised his head to pray; the story continues in the next segment. Al-Ṭhaʿlabī later preserves the report with the same chain.
TABRISI:5:55-56#2/r5.anchor: وكان علي راكعا فأومأ بخنصره اليمنى إليه وكان يتختم فيها

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r1.claim: Abū Dharr continues: the Prophet asks God to expand his heart, ease his task, and appoint ʿAlī as a minister to strengthen him; before the prayer is finished, Gabriel arrives with the command to recite this verse.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r1.anchor: اللهم وأنا محمد نبيك وصفيك اللهم فاشرح لي صدري

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r2.claim: The report says Gabriel told Muḥammad to recite the revelation beginning innamā waliyyukum Allāh wa-rasūluhu wa-lladhīna āmanū.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r2.anchor: أبو ذر: فو الله ما استتم رسول الله الكلمة حتى نزل عليه جبرائيل

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r3.claim: The prophetic prayer for ʿAlī parallels Moses' prayer for Aaron and God's promise in 28:35 to strengthen Moses through his brother.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r3.anchor: سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r4.speaker: الثعلبي، أبو بكر الرازي، الرماني، الطبري، مجاهد، السدي، أبو جعفر، أبو عبد الله، علماء أهل البيت
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r4.claim: Al-Ṭhaʿlabī transmits Abū Dharr's report with the same chain; al-Rāzī, al-Rummānī, al-Ṭabarī, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, reports from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and Ahl al-Bayt scholars say it concerned ʿAlī giving his ring while bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r4.anchor: وروى هذا الخبر أبو إسحاق الثعلبي في تفسيره بهذا الإسناد بعينه

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r5.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse concerns ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and companions after they converted and the Jews cut off their alliance with them.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r5.anchor: الكلبي نزلت في عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r6.speaker: عطاء، عبد الله بن سلام
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r6.claim: In a report from ʿAṭāʾ, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām says he saw ʿAlī give his ring while bowing and therefore they take ʿAlī as their ally.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r6.anchor: في رواية عطاء قال عبد الله بن سلام: يا رسول الله

TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r7.claim: In the account traced through Abū Ṣāliḥ to Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and fellow converts complain that their people shun them, refuse to socialize or intermarry, and leave them without a gathering place; the Prophet recites the verse in response.
TABRISI:5:55-56#3/r7.anchor: أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه ممن قد آمنوا بالنبي

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r1.claim: In the continuation of the Ibn ʿAbbās account, the beggar says the standing man gave him a silver ring while bowing; the Prophet exclaims and recites the verse about God's party being victorious.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r1.anchor: هل أعطاك أحد شيئا " فقال: نعم خاتم من فضة

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r3.speaker: إبراهيم بن الحكم بن ظهير
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr reports that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and companions complained, the verse was revealed, and after the call to prayer the Prophet found ʿAlī giving a silver ring to a petitioner while bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r3.anchor: إبراهيم بن الحكم بن ظهير " أن عبد الله بن سلام أتى رسول الله

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r4.claim: God, His Messenger acting by God's command, and the believers described next are the ones who manage people's interests and whose authority over them requires obedience.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r4.anchor: أي الذي يتولى مصالحكم ويتحقق تدبيركم هو الله تعالى ورسوله

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r5.claim: The believers in view are described as those who establish prayer with its conditions and give zakāt while bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r5.anchor: { الذين يقيمون الصلاة } بشرائطها { ويؤتون } أي ويعطون

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r6.claim: He identifies the believers here as ʿAlī, making this one of the clearest proofs of ʿAlī's immediate imamate after the Prophet.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية من أوضح الدلائل على صحة إمامة علي بعد النبي بلا فصل

TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r7.claim: His argument is that walī means the one more entitled to manage people's affairs and whose obedience is obligatory; once the believers are identified as ʿAlī, the verse explicitly appoints him as imam.
TABRISI:5:55-56#4/r7.anchor: أن لفظة وليكم تفيد من هو أولى بتدبير أموركم ويجب طاعته عليكم

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r1.claim: Innamā is restrictive: it confines the stated guardianship to those named and negates it for others.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r1.anchor: لفظة إنما على ما تقدم ذكره تقتضي التخصيص ونفي الحكم عمن عدا المذكور

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r2.claim: Walāya cannot mean religious friendship or love here, since all believers share that relation and it cannot be exclusive.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r2.anchor: لم يجز حمل لفظة الولي على الموالاة في الدين والمحبة لأنه لا تخصيص في هذا المعنى لمؤمن دون مؤمن آخر

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r3.claim: Once shared friendship is excluded, walāya means authority that entails obligatory obedience over the community.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r3.anchor: لم يبق إلا الوجه الآخر وهو التحقق بالأمور وما يقتضي فرض الطاعة على الجمهور

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r4.claim: A previously cited report through general and particular transmission says the verse came down about Ali when he gave his ring as alms while bowing.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r4.anchor: الرواية الواردة من طريق العامة والخاصة بنزول الآية فيه لما تصدق بخاتمه في حال الركوع

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r5.claim: Those who take wali as authority and imamate identify Ali alone as the verse’s intended referent; no one who accepts that sense assigns it to someone else.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r5.anchor: كل من قال إن المراد بلفظة ولي ما يرجع إلى فرض الطاعة والإمامة ذهب إلى أنه هو المقصود بالآية

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r6.claim: Arabic can use a plural for one person to magnify and honor him, a common usage that answers the objection to a singular referent.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r6.anchor: أهل اللغة قد يعبرون بلفظ الجمع عن الواحد على سبيل التفخيم والتعظيم

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r7.claim: He takes wa-hum rākiʿūn as a circumstantial clause describing the giving of alms; treating it as a general habit of bowing merely repeats the prayer description.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r7.anchor: فلو لم يحمل قوله: { وهم راكعون } على أنه حال من يؤتون الزكاة وحملناه على من صفتهم الركوع كان ذلك كالتكرار غير المفيد

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r8.claim: The address first includes all believers, including the Prophet; naming the Messenger distinguishes him from them, so the later beneficiaries cannot be the addressees or each believer himself.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r8.anchor: فخاطب جميع المؤمنين ودخل في الخطاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وغيره ثم قال ورسوله فأخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من جملتهم

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r9.speaker: الواحدي
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r9.claim: Al-Wahidi says scholars use the verse to show that a small action does not invalidate prayer.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r9.anchor: قال الواحدي واستدل أهل العلم بهذه الآية على أن العمل القليل لا يقطع الصلاة

TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r10.speaker: الواحدي
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi says scholars use the verse to permit giving alms to a petitioner during prayer when the giver intends zakat.
TABRISI:5:55-56#5/r10.anchor: وأن دفع الزكاة إلى السائل في الصلاة جائز مع نية الزكاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Awfi's report, says the verse concerns Abd Allah ibn Ubayy's alliance with Jews and Ubadah ibn al-Samit's disavowal of the Qurayza and Nadir pact in favor of God, His Messenger, and believers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r1.anchor: فقال في رواية العوفي: إنها نازلة في قصة عبد الله بن أبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r2.claim: Jabir reports that Jews shunned Muslims who had converted; Abd Allah ibn Salam said his people would no longer sit with them, so the verse came and they accepted God, His Messenger, and believers as guardians.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r2.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله: إن اليهود هجروا من أسلم منهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r3.claim: On this account, the verse is general: every believer is a guardian of every other believer, as 9:71 says believers are allies of one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r3.anchor: الآية عامة في جميع المؤمنين، فكل مؤمن ولي لكل مؤمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r4.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak take the description of those who pray and give alms as applying to every believer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r4.anchor: وهو قول الحسن في هذه الآية والضحاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says establishing prayer means completing all its required elements, beginning with sound belief in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p433/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: إقامتها: إتمامها بجميع فروضها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the established prayer as obligatory and the bowing as voluntary prayer by night and day; singling out bowing honors it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {الذين يقيمون الصلاة} المفروضة {وهم راكعون} يعني صلاة التطوع بالليل والنهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r2.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r2.claim: Some semanticists say the believers happened to be in these states when the verse came: some had finished prayer and others were bowing; this assumes a general reading, unlike the specific reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r2.anchor: إنهم كانوا في وقت نزول الآية على هذه الصفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ikrima's report, says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة: نزل قوله: {إنما وليكم الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, identifies the believers here as Ali ibn Abi Talib.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r4.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: {والذين آمنوا} يريد علي بن أبي طالب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r5.claim: Abd Allah ibn Salam says they saw Ali give his ring to a needy person while bowing and therefore declared allegiance to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r5.anchor: قال عبد الله بن سلام (¬3): يا رسول الله: إنا رأينا عليا تصدق بخاتمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r6.claim: Abu Dharr recounts a petitioner receiving Ali's ring while Ali was bowing; after prayer, the Prophet prayed for Ali to be his minister and support as Aaron was for Moses, then Gabriel brought this verse. The prayer cites 20:25–32 and 28:35.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r6.anchor: فأومأ إليه بخنصره اليمنى وكان يتختم فيها، فأقبل السائل حتى أخذ الخاتم من خنصره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r7.claim: In Abu Dharr's account, the Prophet invokes Moses' request for an expanded breast, ease in his task, and Aaron as minister, then asks for Ali as his own minister; the cited verses are 20:25–32 and 28:35.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p434/r7.anchor: فاشرح لي صدري، ويسر لي أمري، واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي، عليا أشدد به ظهري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r1.speaker: مجاهد، السدي، عتبة بن أبي حكيم، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r1.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, Utba ibn Abi Hakim, and al-Kalbi say the verse concerns Ali.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r1.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والسدي وعتبة بن أبي حكيم (¬2) والكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Prophet found a petitioner carrying a ring, asked who gave it to him, and learned it was Ali while bowing; when the verse was read, people understood the phrase about bowing as making the reference specific to Ali.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: أذن بلال فخرج رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r3.speaker: أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r3.claim: Scholars infer that a small action does not invalidate prayer and that giving alms to a petitioner during prayer is permitted when intended as zakat; the zakat intention does not conflict with prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r3.anchor: وقال أهل العلم في هذه الآية: إنها تدل على أن العمل القليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r4.claim: Although the occasion of revelation coincided with Ali, the commentators say the verse is general: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Ali answers that Ali is included among believers, not the sole referent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p436/r4.anchor: قال: هم المؤمنون. قلت: فإن ناسا يقولون: هو علي. قال: فعلي من الذين آمنوا

QASHANI:5:55-56/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r1.claim: Qashani allows that God, the Messenger, and believers take charge of you, or that you take God and His Messenger and believers as allies; veiled people cannot be God's allies because of their real opposition.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r1.anchor: أي: يتولى الله ورسوله والمؤمنون إياكم أو لا يتولى الله وأولياءه من الرسول والمؤمنين المحجوبون للتضاد الحقيقي بينهم

QASHANI:5:55-56/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r2.claim: The verse first states the allies' relation to God collectively, then distinguishes Messenger and believers outwardly, as in the testimony verse.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r2.anchor: جمع أولا في إثبات ولايتهم لله مطلقا ثم فصلها بحسب الظاهر، فقال

QASHANI:5:55-56/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r3.claim: Establishing prayer means the prayer of witnessing and presence of the divine essence; giving zakah means the remnant's subsistence.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r3.anchor: صلاة الشهود والحضور الذاتي { ويؤتون } زكاة البقايا

QASHANI:5:55-56/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r4.claim: Bowing is humility in subsistence through God, attributing one's perfections and attributes to God rather than standing arrogantly in them as one's own.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r4.anchor: خاضعون في البقاء بالله بنسبة كمالاتهم وصفاتهم إلى الله

QASHANI:5:55-56/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:55-56/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:55-56/r5.claim: Qashani identifies the verse's revealed referent as the Commander of the Faithful, who professed divine unity after creation's annihilation.
QASHANI:5:55-56/r5.anchor: كأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام النازل في حقه هذا القائل: لا إله إلا الله بعد فناء الخلق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r1.claim: The verse was revealed when Jews ostracized converts. ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam told the Prophet that his people shunned them and swore not to sit with them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r1.anchor: نزلت لما هجر اليهود من أسلم منهم، فقال عبد الله بن سلام: يا رسول الله، إن قومنا قد هجرونا، وأقسموا ألا يجالسونا، فنزلت هذه الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r2.claim: Ibn Salam and the converts accepted God, the Messenger, and the believers as their patrons.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r2.anchor: فقال: رضينا بالله وبرسوله وبالمؤمنين أولياء،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r3.claim: Being bowed here refers to voluntary prayer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:55-57/r3.anchor: وقوله: { وهم راكعون } يعني: صلاة التطوع.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r6.claim: Those seeking honor and independence should seek God’s guardianship and love and support His Messenger and the believers.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r6.anchor: Bu şereflere, bu hürriyete, bu izzet ü istiklâle ermek isteyenler başkalarının değil ancak Allah’ın velâyetine koşmalı

ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r18.claim: The only true guardians, authorities, friends, and helpers are God, then His Messenger following God, and believers following God and His Messenger.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r18.anchor: sizin her mânasıyla velîniz, veliyyü’l-emriniz, muhibbiniz, nâsırınız başkası değil ancak Allah ve Allah’a tebe‘an Resûlü ve Allah’a ve Resûlüne tebe‘an mü’minlerdir.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r19.claim: The believers maintain prayer with its rakʿahs in submission to God and give zakat willingly in obedience to His command; alternatively, they give zakat while bowing.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#2/r19.anchor: Öyle mü’minler ki Allah’a ve Allah’ın emirlerine boyun eğerek rekatlarıyla güzelce namaz kılarlar ve Allah’ın emrine inkıyad ederek hüsn-i rızâlarıyla zekâtlarını verirler, yahut rükûda oldukları hâlde zekât verirler.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r1.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r1.claim: One occasion report, attributed to ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, takes the believers to mean believers generally.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r1.anchor: Evvelkisi Ubâde b. Sâmit hazretlerinin bâlâda nakledilen sözü ve mü’minlerden murad umumdur.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
