ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r2.claim: ʿIkrima’s report identifies Abū Bakr as the referent of “those who believe.”
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r2.anchor: İkrime’nin rivayetine göre Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’dir.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r3.speaker: عطاء، ابن عباس
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies ʿAlī as the referent.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r3.anchor: Üçüncüsü Atâ’nın İbn Abbas’tan rivayetine göre de Hazret-i Ali’dir.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r4.claim: Abū Dharr reports that, after a beggar complained in the mosque, ʿAlī signaled him to take his ring while bowing; the Prophet prayed for ʿAlī as his vizier, and Gabriel then instructed him to recite this verse.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r4.anchor: Ebû Zer’den de “Bir gün mescidde öğle namazını kılmıştık, bir sâil “Yâ Rabbi şâhid ol, Resûlullah’ın mescidine geldim dilendim

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r5.claim: On the basis of the Abū Dharr and Ibn ʿAbbās reports, some take the phrase to denote one specific person, and the Shīʿa use it to argue for ʿAlī’s imamate.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r5.anchor: Bu iki rivayete nazaran وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟’dan murad şahs-ı muayyendir diyenler olmuş ve bundan dolayıdır ki Şîa Hazret-i Ali’nin imameti meselesinde bu âyet ile istidlâl etmek istemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r6.claim: Elmalılı rejects an exclusive referent: Abū Bakr and ʿAlī are certainly among the believers, but they are not the only ones meant.
ELMALILI:5:53-55#3/r6.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Ebû Bekir ve Ali وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ cümlesindendirler fakat yalnız değil.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:55/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:55/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:55/r1.claim: The author renders the believers’ wali as Allah, His Messenger, and believers who faithfully establish prayer and give zakat in submission to God’s command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:55/r1.anchor: Sizin velîniz ancak Allah’tır, peygamberidir, bir de Allah’ın emrine boyun eğerek namazı dosdoğru kılan, zekâtı veren müminlerdir.

BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.claim: The author classifies coordination with God, the Messenger, and believers as a mode of magnification, alongside other pairings of God with the Messenger, angels, or people of knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي

TUSTARI:5:55/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:5:55/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:5:55/r1.claim: God's guardianship is His choice of whom He takes under His care; the Messenger is guardian of believers and must ally with those God and the believers ally with.
TUSTARI:5:55/r1.anchor: قال: ولاية الله تعالى الاختيار لمن استولاه، ثم أعلم الرسول أنه ولي المؤمنين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r1.claim: Jabir says Abdullah ibn Salam complained that Qurayza and Nadir had abandoned him and other converts and refused to socialize; the verse was revealed, and they accepted God, the Messenger, and believers as their patrons.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r1.anchor: قال جابر بن عبد الله: جاء عبد الله بن سلام إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: يا رسول الله إن قوما من قريظة والنضير قد هاجرونا وفارقونا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi adds that the verse's final clause was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, who gave his ring to a beggar while bowing in prayer.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكلبي وزاد: أن آخر الآية نزل في علي بن أبي طالب رضوان الله عليه، لأنه أعطى خاتمه سائلا وهو راكع في الصلاة.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Abdullah ibn Salam and fellow converts complained of Jewish rejection; in the mosque, a beggar identified Ali as the person who gave him a gold ring while bowing, and Muhammad recited the verse ending at 5:56.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p199/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه قد آمنوا، فقالوا: يا رسول الله إن منازلنا بعيدة وليس لنا مجلس ولا متحدث،

DAMGHANI:v1p496/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r11.claim: Walī here denotes religious allegiance or guardianship: God, the Messenger, and the believers are the community's allies in faith.
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r11.anchor: المولى من الولاية في الدين قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

DAMGHANI:v1p209/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r6.claim: Here rukūʿ means bowing in its proper sense, as in the command to bow and prostrate.
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r6.anchor: الثالث : الركوع بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r7.claim: One reported Qurʾānic sense is the prescribed ritual prayer, including each prayer joined with almsgiving.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r1.claim: A walī is someone who takes charge of a person's affairs.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r1.anchor: الولي : من ولي الأمر . فكل من ولى أمرك فهو وليك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p613/r6.claim: Walī can mean a protector or one who prevents harm.

NAHHAS:v2p26/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p26/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p26/r12.claim: The clause is nominal; the Messenger and believers are coordinated with God, and the following relative clause describes the believers.
NAHHAS:v2p26/r12.anchor: ابتداء وخبر ( ورسوله ) عطف ( والذين آمنوا ) كذلك

NAHHAS:v2p26/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p26/r13.speaker: محمد بن علي أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p26/r13.claim: Asked whether the verse means Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muhammad ibn Ali answered that Ali is a believer and took it to include all believers.
NAHHAS:v2p26/r13.anchor: أن محمد بن علي أبا جعفر سئل عن معنى إنما وليكم

NAHHAS:v2p26/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p26/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p26/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar holds that the plural means all believers and their mutual alliance, not imamate; its wording and operation during the Prophet’s lifetime support this.
NAHHAS:v2p26/r14.anchor: وهذا قول بين لأن الذين لجماعة المؤمنين وهذا في تولي المؤمنين

NAHHAS:v2p26/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p26/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p26/r15.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at the right times with all its requirements, as one says someone carries out his work.
NAHHAS:v2p26/r15.anchor: ومعنى يقيمون الصلاة يأتون بها في أوقاتها بجميع حقوقها

SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r1.claim: The clause is nominal: Allāh is the predicate of “your guardian,” and “His Messenger” and “those who believe” are coordinated with the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r1.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر، و " رسوله " و " الذين " عطف على الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the singular walī by presenting God’s guardianship as original and the Messenger’s and believers’ as following it.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: قد ذكرت جماعة فهلا قيل

SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r3.claim: Al-Samīn offers another explanation: the adjective faʿīl can have one form for masculine or feminine, singular, dual, or plural, as in “the men are a friend.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r3.anchor: فعيل، وفعيل وقد نص عليه أهل اللسان

SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r4.claim: He notes that al-Zamakhsharī and others use the same explanation for “the people of Lot are not far from you.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r4.anchor: وقد أجاب الزمخشري وغيره بذلك في قوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s wording “إنما مولاكم” is an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: " إنما مولاكم " وهي تفسير لا قراءة

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r1.claim: One analysis makes “those who establish prayer” a nominative adjective of “those who believe,” describing believers through prayer and almsgiving, the two most excellent branches of faith.

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r2.claim: A second analysis makes the phrase a nominative بدل of “those who believe.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه مرفوع على البدل من " الذين آمنوا "

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r3.claim: A third analysis supplies a new subject: “they are those who establish prayer.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: هم الذين

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r4.claim: A fourth analysis treats the phrase as an explanatory apposition; anything eligible as بدل can be بيان except previously specified cases.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنه عطف بيان لما قبله؛ فإن كل ما جاز أن يكون بدلا جاز أن يكون بيانا

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r5.claim: A fifth analysis makes the phrase accusative under an omitted verb, cutting it off from the preceding dependent construction.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r5.anchor: الخامس: أنه منصوب بإضمار فعل، وهذا الوجه والذي قبله من باب القطع عن التبعية

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r6.claim: The Shaykh asks why al-Zamakhsharī omitted the adjective analysis, which he considers immediate; he also argues that بدل presumes its antecedent could be dropped, impossible for a description on which later descriptions depend.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ:- بعد أن نقل عن الزمخشري وجهي البدل وإضمار المبتدأ فقط - " ولا أدري ما الذي منعه من الصفة

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r7.claim: Al-Samīn disputes the Shaykh: بدل is more immediate, a relative pronoun is not a derivative adjective in form, and he rejects the claim that بدل necessarily treats its antecedent as omitted, citing Sībawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#2/r7.anchor: قلت: لا نسلم أن المتبادر إلى الذهن الوصف بل البدل هو المتبادر

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r1.claim: The clearer analysis coordinates this nominal sentence with the preceding clauses, making it part of the relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r1.anchor: في هذه الجملة وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها معطوفة على ما قبلها من الجمل

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r2.claim: The verse uses a nominal sentence rather than “and they bow” to highlight bowing as the most evident pillar of prayer.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r2.anchor: وجاء بهذه الجملة اسمية دون ما قبلها، فلم يقل " ويركعون " اهتماما بهذا الوصف

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the wāw is circumstantial, with the subject being the wāw in “they give”; rukūʿ means humility toward the poor recipients.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها واو الحال وصاحبها هو واو " يؤتون " والمراد بالركوع الخضوع

SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r4.speaker: علي أمير المؤمنين
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r4.claim: Rukūʿ may be literal: a report says that ʿAlī, Commander of the Faithful, gave his ring in charity while bowing.
SAMIN-DURR:5:55#3/r4.anchor: كما روي عن علي أمير المؤمنين أنه تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع

ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r3.claim: The believers are identified by fully performing prayer with all its obligations, beginning with sound belief in it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r3.anchor: وإقامتها تمامها بجميع فرضها، وأول فروضها صحة الإيمان بها

ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r4.claim: إقامة draws on قوام الأمر; to be قائم with an entrusted task is to fulfill all its due rights.
ZAJJAJ:v2p183/r4.anchor: وهذا كقولك: فلان قائم بعلمه الذي وليه، تأويله إنه يوفي العمل حقوقه

IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r1.speaker: عبادة بن الوليد
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r1.claim: When Banu Qaynuqa fought the Prophet, Abdullah ibn Ubayy supported them. Ubadah ibn al-Samit, their fellow treaty ally, renounced their alliance and declared allegiance to God, His Messenger, and the believers.
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثني أبي إسحاق بن يسار، عن عبادة بن الوليد بن عبادة ابن الصامت

IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq connects 5:55–56 to Ubadah's allegiance to God, His Messenger, and the believers, and his disavowal of Banu Qaynuqa and their pact.
IBNHISHAM:v2p49#2/r3.anchor: وذكر لتولي عبادة بن الصامت الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا، وتبرئه من بني قينقاع وحلفهم وولايتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r1.claim: After prohibiting alliance with Jews and Christians and giving its reason, the verse identifies by restriction those truly entitled to the believers' allegiance.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r1.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه لما قال : لاتتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء وعلله بما علله ذكر عقب ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r2.claim: The contrast means those others ally with one another but are not your allies; reserve allegiance for God, the Messenger, and believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r2.anchor: لأن بعضهم أولياء بعض وليسوا بأوليائكم إنما أولياؤكم الله تعالى ورسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r3.claim: The singular wali despite multiple referents can show that God is the original ally, while the Messenger and believers are allies derivatively.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r3.anchor: وأفرد الولى مع تعدده ليفيد كما قيل : إن الولاية لله تعالى بالأصالة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r4.claim: One parsing supplies an implied وكذلك before the Messenger and believers, preserving God as the grammatical original and the others as derivative allies; al-Alusi rejects treating the singular as simply a plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r4.anchor: فيكون التقدير إنما وليكم الله سبحانه وكذلك رسوله

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r5.claim: An alternative supplies a plural predicate for the full list; the separation emphasizes that the others become allies through God's appointment, so the two analyses converge in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r5.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : التقدير إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا أولياؤكم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r6.claim: Al-Halabi's observation that wali can grammatically serve singular, dual, or plural does not explain the rhetorical reason for changing the wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r6.anchor: أن قول الحلبى ويحتمل وجها آخر وهو أن وليا زنة فعيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r7.claim: The restriction is compatible with the Messenger and believers having delegated allegiance because God alone is the original and true ally.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r7.anchor: لأن الحصر باعتبارأنه سبحانه الولى أصالة وحقيقة وولاية غيره إنما هى بالاسناد اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r8.claim: The description of believers may be appositional to the earlier relative pronoun, an adjective by treating it as a noun, or a nominative or accusative phrase of praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r8.anchor: بدل من الموصول الأول أو صفة له باعتبار إجرائه مجرى الأسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r9.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r9.claim: Abd Allah's reading includes the conjunction waw before those who establish prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r9.anchor: وفى قراءة عبد الله و الذين يقيمون الصلاة بالواو

ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r10.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial clause for the subjects of both verbs, describing them as humble and lowly before God while praying and giving zakah.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p166#2/r10.anchor: حال من فاعل الفعلين أى يعملون ماذكر من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r1.claim: Another view attaches the circumstance only to giving zakah and takes rukuʿ as the prayer bow, showing eagerness and promptness in doing good.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r1.anchor: وقيل : هو حال مخصوصة بايتاء الزكاة والركوع ركوع الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Ibn Salam and fellow converts, shunned by their people and isolated from marriage and conversation, asked the Prophet for help; he declared God and the Messenger their allies, then observed Ali give a silver ring to a beggar while bowing and recited the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r2.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وابن مردويه وغيرهما عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما باسناد متصل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r3.speaker: حسان
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r3.claim: Hassan's poem praises Ali for giving zakah while bowing and says God revealed this special wilayah and recorded it in the scriptures.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r3.anchor: فانشأ حسان رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r4.speaker: الشيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r4.claim: The Shiʿa use the report to argue that the verse was unanimously revealed about Ali, that wali means one with general authority to dispose of affairs, and therefore proves his Imamate and excludes others.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r4.anchor: وا ستبدل الشيعة بها على إمامته كرم الله تعالى وجهه ووجه الاستدلال بها

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r5.claim: In response to the singular referring to one person, grammarians allow plural wording for an eminent individual, magnifying the actor as a community and making the deed a model for every believer; Abraham is called a nation.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167/r5.anchor: فقد جاء فى غير ماموضع وذكر علماء العربية أنه يكون لفائدتين : تعظيم الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r1.claim: The first Sunni response is reductio: the same exclusive reading would disqualify Hasan, Husayn, and the later twelve Imams, harming the Shiʿi argument more than the Sunni position.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r1.anchor: الأول النقض بأن هذا الدليل كما يدل بزعمهم على نفى إمامة الأئمة المتقدمين

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r2.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r2.claim: The restriction cannot be made relative to earlier leaders if it is to prove exclusive authority, and later Imams do not all share the stated qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r2.anchor: ولايمكن أن يقال : الحصر إضافى بالنسبة إلى من تقدمه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r3.speaker: الشيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r3.claim: The Shiʿi reply limits the exclusive authority to Ali's own period as Imam, not the periods of Hasan, Husayn, and those after them.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r3.anchor: وإن أجابوا عن النقض بأن المراد حصر الولاية فى الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه فى بعض الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r4.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r4.claim: The Sunni response accepts that Ali had general authority during his own imamate, while denying that it held during the three caliphs before him or his successors afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r4.anchor: فمرحبا بالوفاق إذ مذهبنا أيضا أن الولاية العامة كانت له وقت كونه إماما

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r5.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r5.claim: An argument that subordination to earlier caliphs diminished Ali, unlike the later imamate of his descendants, changes the proof: it assumes that prior subordination is a defect and that a rightful ruler can never be deficient, neither of which follows from the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r5.anchor: هذا فرار وانتقال إلى استدلال آخر ليس مفهوما من الآية إذ مبناه على مقدمتين

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r6.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r6.claim: The subordination argument is also challenged by Hasan and Husayn under Ali's authority and by Ali under the Prophet's authority.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r6.anchor: على أن هذا الاستدلال منقوض بالسبطين زمن ولاية الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r7.speaker: محمد الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r7.claim: A second Sunni response denies consensus about the occasion: al-Naqqash reports Muhammad al-Baqir as saying the verse concerned the Emigrants and Helpers, with Ali included among them.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p167#2/r7.anchor: فقد اختلف علماء التفسير فى ذلك فروى أبو بكر النقاش صاحب التفسير المشهور عن محمد الباقر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r1.speaker: الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r1.claim: Al-Baqir reports a similar account, which al-Alusi says better fits the verse’s plural wording; he names Abu Nuʿaym, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim among its transmitters or sources.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r1.anchor: عن الباقر رضى الله تعالى عنه أيضا نحو ذلك وهذه الرواية أوفق بصيغ الجمع فى الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r2.claim: A group of exegetes report from ʿIkrima that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r2.anchor: وروى جمع من المفسرين عن عكرمة أنها نزلت فى شأن أبى بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r3.claim: Al-Alusi prefers wali as helper because the context strengthens believers, consoles them, and removes their fear of apostates.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r3.anchor: بل المراد به الناصر لأن الكلام فى تقوية قلوب المؤمنين وتسليها وإزالة الخوف عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r4.claim: The following prohibition on taking Jews, Christians, and unbelievers as allies shows that wali here means ally or supporter, since they were not made supreme imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r4.anchor: من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء آب عن حمل الولى على مايساوى الإمام الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r5.claim: The exclusivity particle fits support and affection, where disagreement existed at revelation, rather than general imamate, over which there was then no dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r5.anchor: وكلمة إنما المفيدة للحصر تقتضى ذلك المعنى أيضا لأن الحصر يكون فيما يحتمل اعتقاد الشركة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r6.speaker: المرتضى وابن المطهر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r6.claim: Al-Murtada and Ibn al-Mutahhar are cited for treating the plural wording as general or equivalent to a general expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r6.anchor: كما ذكره المرتضى فى الذريعة واين المطهر فى النهاية

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r7.claim: On that argument, general authority belongs to multiple men including Ali; reading the general wording as a specific reference departs from the default without necessity.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r7.anchor: مفاد الآية حينئذ حصر الولاية العامة لرجال متعددين يدخل فيهم الأمير

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r8.claim: The verse does not state that charity was given during ritual prayer-bowing; rukūʿ can mean humility and submission, as in Arabic usage and Quranic examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r8.anchor: لجواز أن يكون الركوع بمعنى التخشع والتذلل لابالمعنى المعروف فى عرف أهل الشرع

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r9.claim: A poetic line uses rukūʿ for becoming humbled by changing fortune, supporting a nonritual sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r9.anchor: لاتهين الفقير علك أن تركع يوما والدهر قد رفعه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r10.claim: Taking rukūʿ nonritually is no less plausible than taking zakat, paired with prayer, as this particular almsgiving, an interpretation the Imami argument requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r10.anchor: وليس حمل الركوع فى الآية على غير معناه الشرعى بأبعد من حمل الزكاة المقرونة بالصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r11.speaker: بعض منا أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r11.claim: An unnamed Sunni argues that ritual bowing as a circumstance of paying zakat weakens the sense of establishing prayer: even small extraneous movements detract from its perfection, so this is an unsuitable reading of divine speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p168/r11.anchor: إن حمل الركوع على معناه الشرعى وجعل الجملة حالا من فاعل يأتون

ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r1.speaker: ابن الجوزى
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r1.claim: Asked how Ali could give a ring while praying, Ibn al-Jawzi answers in verse that love’s intoxication need not distract from the companion or other people and can permit an act of the alert.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r1.anchor: كيف تصدق على كرم الله تعالى وجهه بالخاتم وهو فى الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r2.speaker: الشيخ إبراهيم الكردى
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Kurdi says the proof misses the disputed point: the Imami reading cannot concern the Prophet’s lifetime, since imamate is deputyship after his death; with no stated delay, it could mean Ali after the three earlier imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r2.anchor: الشيخ إبراهيم الكردى قدس سره عن أصل الاستدلال

ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r3.speaker: صاحب إظهار الحق
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r3.claim: The author reports Izhar al-Haqq’s argument that the joined command makes love and allegiance to the qualified believers obligatory like love of God and the Messenger; since this cannot mean every Muslim, and some enmity is permitted or required, it must mean a subset identified as Ali.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r3.anchor: صاحب إظهار الحق قد بلغ سعيه الغاية القصوى فى تصحيح الاستدلال

ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r4.claim: Even granting the premises, they do not entail the specific conclusion; faith-based allegiance to believers is general and directed to their faith, so hostility for another reason does not negate it.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p169/r4.anchor: ويرد عليه أنه مع تسليم المقدمات أين اللزوم بين الدليل والمدعى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r1.claim: The verse saying believing men and women are allies of one another confirms that mutual allegiance is general, not limited to Ali.

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r2.claim: The much larger number of unbelievers does not prevent treating them collectively; likewise, many believers can be considered under the unity of their shared description.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r2.anchor: عن معادات الكفار وكيف الأمر فيها وهم أضعاف المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r3.claim: The three allegiances do not stand at one rank: God is primary, the Messenger subordinate, and believers subordinate to him; conjunction shares the ruling, not its aspect or relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r3.anchor: والمحذور كون الموالاة الثلاثة فى مرتبة واحدة وليس إذ الأولى أصل والثانية تبع

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r4.claim: The joined wording in 12:108 links a duty for the Prophet with a recommended act for his followers; conjunction in expression does not require identical legal force.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r4.anchor: القران فى النظم لايوجب القران فى الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r5.speaker: حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Hudhayfa that people asked the Prophet to appoint a successor; he warned that disobeying an appointee would bring punishment and instructed them to trust Hudhayfa’s reports and follow ʿAbd Allah’s recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r5.anchor: فقد روى الترمذى عن حذيفة أنهم قالوا : يارسول الله لو استخلفت

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r6.speaker: على
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r6.claim: Ahmad reports from Ali that, when asked who should be appointed after the Prophet, he named Abu Bakr and Umar’s virtues and said Ali would guide rightly, though he did not think they would choose him.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r6.anchor: فقد أخرج أحمد عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : قيل : يارسول الله من نؤمر بعدك

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r7.claim: Al-Alusi says asking about succession alone does not establish uncertainty; that would require subsequent consultation or dispute after the Prophet answered, which is not reported.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r7.anchor: وفيه أن محض السؤال والاستفسار لايتقضى وقوع التردد

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r8.claim: Even if uncertainty existed, the reports do not establish whether it preceded or followed the verse, was connected to its revelation, or was incidental; possibility is not proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r8.anchor: وأيضا لوسلمنا التردد ولكن كيف العلم بأنه بعد الآية أو قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r9.claim: The second hadith conflicts with exclusivity whichever came first: a prior verse would make the Prophet’s answer contrary to it, while a later verse would conflict with a report that cannot be abrogated; chronology is unknown.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r9.anchor: فى مقام السؤال عن المستحق للخلافة ذكر الشيخين

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r10.claim: If a solitary report is inadmissible to establish imamate, it is also inadmissible to establish the uncertainty needed for this argument; the first report also favors leaving appointment, which the claimants reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r10.anchor: الحديث خبر الواحد وهو غير مقبول فى باب الامامة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r11.speaker: الطبرسى
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r11.claim: Al-Tabrisi argues that the address covers all believers, then names the Messenger and believers as guardians, so the addressed group differs from the recipients of guardianship; otherwise each believer would be his own guardian.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p170/r11.anchor: الطبرسى فى مجمع البيان وجها آخر غير ماذكره صاحب إظهار الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r1.claim: The verse means believers are guardians of one another, not that each is his own guardian; ordinary plural expressions such as forbidding people to backbite people work the same way.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r1.anchor: صوموا يوم يصوم الناس ولايختلج فى القلب أنه أمر لكل أحد أن يصوم يوم يصوم الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r2.claim: The previously discussed occasion identifies Ibn Salam and his companions as the addressees, though the occasion does not restrict the verse’s general wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r2.anchor: ظاهر فى أن المخاطب بذلك ابن سلام وأصحابه وعليه لاإشكال

ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r3.claim: Al-Alusi concludes that the verse does not establish Ali’s caliphate in the specific way the Imamis claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p171/r3.anchor: فالآية على كل حال لاتدل على خلافة الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه على الوجه الذى تزعمه الامامية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed concerning Ubada ibn al-Samit and Abdullah ibn Ubayy after Ubada disavowed the Jews and declared allegiance to God, the Messenger, and believers; the passage begins at 5:51.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها نزلت في عبادة بن الصامت وعبد الله بن أبي بن سلول حين تبرأ عبادة من اليهود،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r2.claim: Jabir reports that Abdullah ibn Salam said Qurayza and Nadir had shunned his people; the verse was revealed, and they accepted God, His Messenger, and believers as allies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r2.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله: جاء عبد الله بن سلام إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله إن قومنا قريظة والنضير قد هجرونا وفارقونا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.claim: In the first occasion-of-revelation interpretation, “while bowing” refers to voluntary prayer at night and during the day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا التأويل أراد بقوله: {وهم راكعون} صلاة التطوع بالليل والنهار، قاله ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the believer as Ali, who gave his ring to a beggar while bowing in the mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: قوله: "والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون"، أراد به علي بن أبي طالب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak, as reported by Jubayr, says believers are allies of one another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.anchor: وقال جوبير عن الضحاك في قوله: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا} قال: هم المؤمنون بعضهم أولياء بعض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.claim: Al-Baqir says the verse was revealed about believers; when told it was said to concern Ali, he replied that Ali is one of the believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا} نزلت في المؤمنين، فقيل له: إن أناسا يقولون إنها نزلت في علي

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r1.claim: After forbidding alliance with unbelievers, the verse names those truly worthy of it: God is the original guardian, while the Messenger and believers hold that role dependently.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r1.anchor: لما نهى عن موالاة الكفرة ذكر عقيبه من هو حقيق بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r2.claim: The prayer and almsgiving clauses modify the believers as an adjective or stand in apposition; they may also be accusative or nominative as praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r2.anchor: صفة للذين آمنوا فإنه جرى مجرى الاسم

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r3.claim: The preferred sense is that they are humble in their prayer and almsgiving.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r4.claim: An alternative ties the phrase to giving alms while bowing in prayer, out of eagerness to do good.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r4.anchor: في حال ركوعهم في الصلاة حرصا على الإحسان ومسارعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r5.claim: A report says it was revealed about ʿAlī: a petitioner asked him for help as he prayed, and he gave the petitioner his ring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r5.anchor: نزلت في علي رضي الله عنه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r6.speaker: الشيعة
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r6.claim: The Shiʿites cite the verse for ʿAlī’s imamate, taking walī to mean the one who governs affairs and is entitled to exercise authority.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r6.anchor: استدل بها الشيعة على إمامته زاعمين أن المراد بالولي

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r7.claim: The apparent sense is the one given above, and reading a plural as one person is also nonapparent; if revealed about ʿAlī, the plural may invite others to emulate him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r7.anchor: والظاهر ما ذكرناه مع أن حمل الجمع على الواحد أيضا خلاف الظاهر

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r8.claim: On this interpretation, a small action during prayer does not invalidate it, and voluntary charity can be called zakāh.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:55/r8.anchor: الفعل القليل في الصلاة لا يبطلها وأن صدقة التطوع تسمى زكاة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r4.claim: Since the preceding passage negated the disbelievers’ allegiance as love, aid, and closeness, it concludes that true allegiance is exclusively God’s and His allies’.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r4.anchor: ولما نفى سبحانه ولايتهم بمعنى المحبة وبمعنى النصرة وبمعنى القرب بكل اعتبار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r5.claim: God alone is truly able to do what a protecting ally must do; everyone else can act only through Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r5.anchor: ولا يقدر غيره على شيء من ذلك إلا به سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r6.claim: God’s own allegiance is known through the allegiance of His allies; the Messenger is named first as the most deserving, and attachment to God marks his exalted rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r6.anchor: من تعرف ولايته سبحانه بولايتهم بادئا بأحقهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r7.claim: Prayer establishes connection with the Creator, while almsgiving is beneficence toward created beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r7.anchor: أي تمكينا لوصلتهم بالخالق { ويؤتون الزكاة } إحسانا إلى الخلائق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r8.claim: One parsing coordinates ‘while bowing’ with establishing prayer, describing believers who bow; the author notes Jews and Christians do not bow in prayer.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r9.claim: Alternatively, ‘while bowing’ is a circumstantial clause describing the person giving alms.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r9.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون حالا من فاعل الإيتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r10.speaker: أسباب النزول
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r10.claim: A report on the occasion says the verse was revealed about ʿAlī, who gave his ring to a petitioner while bowing.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r10.anchor: أنها نزلت في علي رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r11.claim: The wording is plural despite the single reported occasion to encourage others to emulate the good deed promptly and prevent treating it as exclusive to ʿAlī.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p483/r11.anchor: وجمع وإن كان السبب واحدا ترغيبا في مثل فعله نم فعل الخير والتعجيل به

DURR-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.speaker: عطية بن سعد
DURR-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.claim: Atiyya ibn Sad reports that the verse about the believers’ guardianship was revealed concerning Ubada ibn al-Samit.
DURR-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.anchor: عن عطية بن سعد قال: نزلت في عبادة بن الصامت

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ali gave his ring while bowing; when the Prophet asked the beggar who gave it, he answered, the one bowing, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies Ali ibn Abi Talib as the person concerning whom the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله} الآية قال: نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r3.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r3.claim: Ammar says Ali gave a ring to a beggar while bowing in voluntary prayer; the Prophet recited the verse and declared Ali the mawla of whoever has him as mawla.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r3.anchor: عن عمار بن ياسر قال: وقف بعلي سائل وهو راكع في صلاة تطوع

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r4.claim: Ali reports that the verse came to the Prophet at home; in the mosque a beggar confirmed that only the bowing Ali had given him a ring.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال نزلت هذه الآية على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيته

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r5.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r5.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl reports that the verse was revealed after Ali gave his ring in charity while bowing.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r5.anchor: عن سلمة بن كهيل قال: تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r6.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed concerning Ali, who gave charity while bowing.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله} الآية نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r7.speaker: السدي وعتبة بن حكيم
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r7.claim: Al-Suddi and Utba ibn Hakim give the same report that the verse concerns Ali’s charity while bowing.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن السدي وعتبة بن حكيم مثله

DURR-FULL:v3p104/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abdullah ibn Salam and fellow converts complained of hostility and isolation from their former community; this verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v3p104/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أتى عبد الله بن سلام ورهط معه من أهل الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r2.speaker: أبو رافع
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r2.claim: Abu Rafi says he protected the sleeping Prophet from a snake during revelation; on waking, the Prophet recited the verse and praised God for completing Ali’s blessings.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r2.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه وأبو نعيم عن أبي رافع قال دخلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو نائم يوحى إليه فإذا حية

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ali gave a beggar his ring while bowing; the verse was revealed for the believers, with Ali first among them.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان علي بن أبي طالب قائما يصلي فمر سائل وهو راكع

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses taking God, the Messenger, and the believers as patrons to mean that whoever submits to Islam has taken them as patrons.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إنما وليكم الله} الآية قال: يعني من أسلم فقد تولى الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r5.claim: Asked whether the believers meant Ali, Abu Jafar answered that Ali is one of the believers.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r5.anchor: عن أبي جعفر أنه سئل عن هذه الآية من الذين آمنوا قال: الذين آمنوا

DURR-FULL:v3p106/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r6.claim: Abu Jafar identifies the believers as Muhammad’s Companions and says Ali is among them.
DURR-FULL:v3p106/r6.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن أبي سليمان قال: سألت أبا جعفر محمد بن علي

DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r1.claim: Abdullah’s recitation includes the clause about believers who establish prayer, omitting the following charity and bowing clause in this quoted reading.
DURR-FULL:v3p106#2/r1.anchor: عن جرير بن مغيرة قال: كان في قراءة عبد الله {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة}

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that whoever submits is taken as a patron by God, His Messenger, and the believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : انما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين امنوا يعني : انه من اسلم تولاه الله ورسوله والذين امنوا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r2.claim: Asked whether the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar answered that ʿAlī is one of the believers named by it.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r2.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن ابى سليمان قال : سالت أبا جعفر محمد بن علي عن قوله : انما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين امنوا قلت : نزلت في علي قال : علي من الذين امنوا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse means the believers, with ʿAlī among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r3.anchor: عن السدى قوله : انما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين امنوا قال : هم المؤمنون وعلي منهم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r4.speaker: عقبة بن أبي حكيم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r4.claim: ʿUqba ibn Abī Ḥakīm identifies the believers meant here as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r4.anchor: عن عقبة بن ابى حكيم في قوله : انما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين امنوا قال : علي بن ابى طالب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r5.speaker: الزهري
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī explains establishing prayer as performing the five daily prayers at their appointed times.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r5.anchor: قال الزهري : اقامتها : ان تصلي الاوقات الخمس لوقتها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r6.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r6.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl reports that ʿAlī gave his ring in charity while bowing, and the verse was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r6.anchor: ثنا موسى بن قيس الحضرمي عن سلمة بن كهيل قال : تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع فنزلت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r7.speaker: عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r7.claim: ʿAṭiyya says the verse beginning “Your patron is only God and His Messenger” was revealed concerning ʿUbāda.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1162/r7.anchor: عن أبيه عن عطية قال : في عبادة نزلت انما وليكم لله ورسوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r1.claim: The sentence reconnects to the prohibition in 5:51 after 5:54's parenthetical statement, and supplies its rationale by affirming believers' guardianship by God and His Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r1.anchor: إلى آخرها متصلة بجملة { يأيها الذين آمنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r2.claim: Since God and His Messenger are the believers' guardians, they should not take God's enemies as guardians; the sentence reinforces the prohibition and praises believers by affirming the opposite loyalty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r2.anchor: لأن ولايتهم لله ورسوله مقررة عندهم فمن كان الله وليه لا تكون أعداء الله أولياءه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r3.claim: The affirmative report functions as a command to confirm and maintain this loyalty; إنما effects a genuine restriction of attribute to subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r3.anchor: والقصر المستفاد من ( إنما ) قصر صفة على موصوف قصرا حقيقيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r4.claim: The believers' guardianship means that believers are guardians of one another, as stated in 9:71.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r4.anchor: ومعنى كون الذين آمنوا أولياء للذين آمنوا أن المؤمنين بعضهم أولياء بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p239/r5.claim: The prayer and almsgiving descriptions are attributes of the believers, included to praise them; the same praise continues in وهم راكعون.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r1.claim: وهم راكعون is coordinated with the preceding attribute; it may also be parsed as a circumstantial clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وهم راكعون } معطوف على الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r2.claim: The apparent sense is worshippers who pray, with راكعون referring to prayer generally rather than the bodily bowing element.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r2.anchor: إذ المراد ب { راكعون } مصلون لا آتون بالجزء من الصلاة المسمى بالركوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r3.claim: One possible specification is voluntary prayers: they perform the five obligatory prayers and also draw near through supererogatory ones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r3.anchor: فوجه هذا العطف : إما بأن المراد بالركوع ركوع النوافل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r4.claim: Alternatively, the nominal clause indicates persistence: they continually maintain prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r4.anchor: إما المراد به ما تدل عليه الجملة الإسمية من الدوام والثبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r5.claim: Mentioning almsgiving after prayer singles it out for praise, as is the Quran's usual practice.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r6.claim: Abu Bakr inferred that one may fight those who separate the obligation of prayer from almsgiving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r6.anchor: وهو الذي استنبطه أبو بكر رضي الله عنه إذ قال : ( لأقاتلن من فرق بين الصلاة والزكاة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r7.claim: The clause also praises believers for not falling behind in performing prayer; the conjunction links one attribute to another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r7.anchor: بأنهم لا يتخلفون عن أداء الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r8.claim: The word may also mean humble or reverent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل الجملة حالا . ويراد بالركوع الخشوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r9.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r9.claim: Some commentators take the clause as a state of the pronoun in يؤتون, making it describe almsgiving while bowing; Ibn Ashur says this reading has no sensible meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r9.anchor: ومن المفسرين من جعل { وهم راكعون } حالا من ضمير { يؤتون الزكاة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r10.speaker: الحاكم وابن مردويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r10.claim: Their report says Ibn Salam and fellow Jewish converts complained of distance and Jewish hostility; later, an asker said Ali had given him a silver ring while praying, after which the Prophet recited the verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r10.anchor: روى الحاكم وابن مردويه : جاء ابن سلام ( أي عبد الله ) ونفر من قومه الذين آمنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir judges all versions of the Ali-in-prayer report unsound because their chains are weak and narrators unknown.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r11.anchor: قال ابن كثير : وليس يصح شيء منها بالكلية لضعف أسانيدها وجهالة رجالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya expresses reservations about the report that explains almsgiving as occurring during bowing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : وفي هذا القول ، أي الرواية ، نظر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r13.claim: The circumstantial reading is senseless if it means giving alms during bowing; that interpretation was built on reports whose versions are weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r13.anchor: وليس فيه معنى ، إذ تؤتى الزكاة في حالة الركوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r14.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r14.claim: Another reported view says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r14.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r15.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p240/r15.claim: A further reported view says the verse was revealed about the Emigrants and Helpers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.claim: The address continues the command not to take Jews and Christians as allies in 5:51; innama restricts the guardianship named here, and wali is a generic noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.anchor: الخطاب بقوله: إنما وليكم الله الآية للقوم الذين قيل لهم لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء [المائدة: 51]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads inna-mawlākum Allah, using mawlākum.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.claim: The believers are those truly faithful rather than hypocrites, who establish obligatory prayer with all its conditions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.anchor: أي ومن آمن من الناس حقيقة لا نفاقا وهم الذين يقيمون الصلاة المفروضة بجميع شروطها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.claim: Zakat here broadly includes obligatory alms, voluntary charity, and every good deed, which increases good works and purifies a person from sin; believers give according to their capacity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.anchor: وهي هنا لفظ عام للزكاة المفروضة وللتطوع بالصدقة ولكل أفعال البر، إذ هي تنمية للحسنات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads with an additional conjunction: amanu wa-alladhina yuqimuna.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «آمنوا والذين يقيمون» بواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.claim: The clause wa-hum raki'un is coordinated with the preceding clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وهم راكعون جملة معطوفة على جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.claim: The majority understand this as describing abundant prayer: rukūʿ is singled out as a major pillar and humble posture standing for the whole prayer, as “the bowing and prostrating” does in 2:125.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.anchor: وخص الركوع بالذكر لكونه من أعظم أركان الصلاة، وهو هيئة تواضع فعبر به عن جميع الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerns believers generally, but happened to coincide with Ali ibn Abi Talib giving his ring to a beggar while bowing in the mosque.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.anchor: قال السدي: هذه الآية في جمع المؤمنين ولكن عليا بن أبي طالب مر به سائل وهو راكع في المسجد فأعطاه خاتمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet, after the verse was revealed, asked a beggar whether anyone had given him anything; the beggar described a silver ring given by a praying man while bowing, and the Prophet identified Ali and recited the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.anchor: وروي في ذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من بيته وقد نزلت عليه الآية فوجد مسكينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r1.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil agrees, that the verse followed Abdullah ibn Salam and companions' complaint of hostility and distance from the Prophet's companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r1.anchor: رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r2.claim: In the same account, Ali gave a beggar his silver ring while bowing, and the Prophet recited the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r2.anchor: وهو راكع فقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r3.claim: Al-Awfi reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse concerned Ubadah ibn al-Samit after he renounced his alliance with Jewish allies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r3.anchor: والثاني أن عبادة بن الصامت لما تبرأ من حلفائه اليهود نزلت هذه الآية في حقه رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r4.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r4.anchor: والثالث أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse concerns Muslims who have passed and those yet to come.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p382/r5.anchor: والرابع أنها نزلت فيمن مضى من المسلمين ومن بقي منهم قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r1.claim: One interpretation is that they give alms while bowing, as Ali did when he gave his ring.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنهم فعلوا ذلك في ركوعهم وهو تصدق علي عليه السلام بخاتمه في ركوعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r2.claim: Another interpretation describes their usual practice of giving alms and performing the bow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r2.anchor: والثاني أن من شأنهم إيتاء الزكاة وفعل الركوع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r3.claim: The first explanation takes rukūʿ as the actual prayer bow; Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that the verse came down while they were bowing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه نفس الركوع على ما روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وقيل إن الآية نزلت وهم في الركوع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas understands rukūʿ as voluntary prayer by night and day, with the bow singled out for honor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه صلاة التطوع بالليل والنهار وإنما أفرد الركوع بالذكر تشريفا له وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r5.claim: The third explanation takes rukūʿ as humility and submission; the cited poem says one may bow to a poor person whom time later raises.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p383/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه الخضوع والخشوع وأنشدوا لا تذل الفقير علك أن تر كع يوما والدهر قد رفعه ذكره الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r2.claim: The Jews are not the believers’ allies; their allegiance belongs to God, His Messenger, and the believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r2.anchor: أي: ليس اليهود بأوليائكم، بل ولايتكم راجعة إلى الله ورسوله والمؤمنين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r3.claim: The believers establish prayer, Islam’s greatest pillar, for God alone, and give zakat, the right of people and help for the weak and needy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r3.anchor: أي: المؤمنون المتصفون بهذه الصفات، من إقام الصلاة التي هي أكبر أركان الإسلام، وهي له وحده (2) لا شريك له،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r4.claim: Some take this phrase as a circumstantial clause modifying zakat-giving, implying that charity while bowing is superior; Ibn Kathir rejects that implication because no known legal authority holds it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r4.anchor: فقد توهم بعضهم أن هذه الجملة في موضع الحال من قوله: {ويؤتون الزكاة} أي: في حال ركوعهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some have cited a report that the verse came down about Ali when a beggar passed as he bowed and he gave him his ring.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r5.anchor: حتى إن بعضهم ذكر في هذا أثرا عن علي بن أبي طالب: أن هذه الآية نزلت فيه: [ذلك] (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r6.speaker: عتبة بن أبي حكيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r6.claim: ʿUtba ibn Hakim interprets those named as the believers and Ali ibn Abi Talib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r6.anchor: عن عتبة بن أبي حكيم في قوله: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا} قال: هم المؤمنون وعلي بن أبي طالب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r7.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r7.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl reports that Ali gave his ring in charity while bowing and the verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r7.anchor: عن سلمة بن كهيل قال: تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع، فنزلت: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about Ali giving charity while bowing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r8.anchor: حدثنا غالب بن عبيد الله، سمعت مجاهدا يقول في قوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p137#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through his son’s son Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, says the verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid is not an authoritative transmitter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r1.anchor: عبد الوهاب بن مجاهد لا يحتج به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r2.claim: A report through al-Dahhak says Ali gave a ring to a beggar while bowing and the verse was revealed; Ibn Kathir notes al-Dahhak never met Ibn Abbas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس قال: كان علي بن أبي طالب قائما يصلي، فمر سائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r3.claim: A report through the abandoned transmitter al-Kalbi says the Prophet asked a beggar who gave him charity and learned it was Ali while bowing; Ibn Kathir says this chain is not reliable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r3.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المسجد، والناس يصلون،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says the reports from Ali, Ammar ibn Yasir, and Abu Rafi on this occasion are all unsound because their chains are weak and their narrators unknown.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r4.anchor: ثم رواه ابن مردويه، من حديث علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، نفسه، وعمار بن ياسر، وأبي رافع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report from Maymun ibn Mihran, says the verse concerns the believers, with Ali first among them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r5.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله} نزلت في المؤمنين، وعلي بن أبي طالب أولهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r6.claim: Asked who the believers are, Abu Jaʿfar answers that they are the believers; when told the verse was said to concern Ali, he replies that Ali is one of the believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r6.anchor: عن أبي جعفر قال: سألته عن هذه [الآية] (1) {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerns all believers, while noting that Ali gave his ring to a beggar as he bowed in the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r7.anchor: وقال أسباط، عن السدي: نزلت هذه الآية في جميع المؤمنين، ولكن علي بن أبي طالب مر به سائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says that whoever embraces Islam has taken God, His Messenger, and the believers as allies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p138/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة الوالبي، عن ابن عباس: من أسلم فقد تولى الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the preceding verses were revealed about ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who renounced his Jewish alliance and accepted the guardianship of God, the Messenger, and the believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p139/r1.anchor: أن هذه الآيات كلها نزلت في عبادة بن الصامت، رضي الله عنه، حين تبرأ من حلف يهود،

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r3.claim: Mawla here is the one who undertakes to support the person allied with him.

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r5.claim: When ʿUbada ibn al-Samit broke with the Jews and allied with God and His Messenger, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy opposed him; this occasion is attributed to ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r5.anchor: نزلت الآية في عبادة بن الصامت لما تبرأ من اليهود، وتولى الله ورسوله

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r6.claim: Another occasion was the Prophet's decision to fight Banu Qaynuqa, allies of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy; Saʿd and ʿUbada ibn al-Samit disavowed them while ʿAbd Allah opposed the decision.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r6.anchor: قتل بني قينقاع، وكانوا حلفاء عبد الله بن أبي، وسعد بن عبادة وعبادة بن الصامت

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r7.speaker: جابر
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r7.claim: When the Jews shunned the newly converted ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, he complained to the Prophet, then declared himself content with God, His Messenger, and the believers as allies.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r7.anchor: وقيل: لما أسلم عبد الله بن سلام هجره اليهود من موالاته وكلامه ومجالسته

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r8.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r8.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say the verse was revealed when ʿAli gave his ring as charity while bowing.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r8.anchor: تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع، عن مجاهد والسدي

JISHUMI:v3p2002/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r9.speaker: أبو ذر
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r9.claim: A similar long report from Abu Dharr says a beggar received ʿAli's ring while ʿAli was bowing and gestured with his ring-bearing right pinkie; the author says God knows whether the report is sound, and it quotes Moses' prayer.
JISHUMI:v3p2002/r9.anchor: وروي نحوه عن أبي ذر في حديث طويل - الله أعلم بصحته - أن سائلا سأل في المسجد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r1.claim: After forbidding allegiance to those who must be opposed, the passage names those who must be allied.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r1.anchor: عقب النهي عن موالاة من تجب معاداتهم ذكر من تجب موالاتهم بقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r2.claim: Innamā makes allegiance to God, His Messenger, and believers exclusive and obligatory.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r3.claim: The singular walī begins with God’s intrinsic guardianship, then adds the Prophet and believers derivatively; using plural awliyāʾ would erase this distinction between origin and dependent status.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r3.anchor: أصل الكلام إنما وليكم الله فجعلت الولاية لله على طريق الأصالة ثم نظم في سلك اثباتها له إثباتها لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين على سبيل التبع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r4.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( إنما مولاكم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r5.claim: Alladhīna yuqīmūna may be nominative as an appositive to alladhīna āmanū, a predicate of an implied ‘they are,’ or accusative as praise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r5.anchor: الرفع على البدل من الذين آمنوا أو على هم الذين يقيمون أو النصب على المدح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r6.claim: The description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocrites and from those whose hearts assent but whose deeds fall short.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#3/r6.anchor: وفيه تمييز للخلص من الذين آمنوا نفاقا أو واطأت قلوبهم ألسنتهم الا انهم مفرطون في العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r1.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they know this while bowing, meaning in humility, submission, and lowliness before God during prayer and almsgiving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r1.anchor: الواو فيه للحال اي يعلمون ذلك في حال الركوع وهو الخشوع والإخبات والتواضع لله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r2.claim: An alternative takes the circumstantial phrase with giving zakat: they give it while bowing in prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r2.anchor: وقيل هو حال من يؤتون الزكاة بمعنى يؤتونها في حال ركوعهم في الصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r3.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about ʿAlī, who gave a petitioner his ring while bowing; al-Zamakhsharī calls it baseless.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r3.anchor: 357 أنها نزلت في علي كرم الله وجهه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع في صلاته فطرح له خاتمه + باطل لا أصل له +

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r4.claim: The story supposes the ring was on ʿAlī’s little finger, so removing it required no substantial movement that would invalidate prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r4.anchor: كأنه كان مرجا في خنصره فلم يتكلف لخلعه كثير عما تفسد بمثله صلاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r5.claim: Plural wording for a single reported occasion encourages others to imitate the act and attain its reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r5.anchor: جيء به على لفظ الجمع وإن كان السبب فيه رجلا واحدا ليرغب الناس في مثل فعله فينالوا مثل ثوابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r6.claim: The wording also portrays believers as exceptionally eager for charity and attentive to the poor, not postponing urgent help even while praying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p681#4/r6.anchor: ولينبه على ان سجية المؤمنين يجب أن تكون على هذه الغاية من الحرص على البر والإحسان وتفقد الفقراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions after they complained to the Prophet about Jewish hostility.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أنها نزلت في عبد الله بن سلام ومن أسلم معه من أصحابه حين شكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r6.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r6.claim: The other reported occasion concerns Ubada ibn al-Samit, who renounced his Jewish alliance and declared that he would take God and His Messenger as protectors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r6.anchor: والثاني : أنها نزلت في عبادة بن الصامت حين تبرأ من حلف اليهود وقال : أتولى الله ورسوله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r7.claim: Mujahid identifies the people who gave alms while bowing as Ali, who gave charity during his bowing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أنه علي , تصدق وهو راكع , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Suddi say the description applies generally to all believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنها عامة في جميع المؤمنين , قاله الحسن , والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r9.claim: The phrase may say they give charity during prayer's bowing, or that the verse was revealed while they were bowing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r9.anchor: وفي قوله : { وهم راكعون } ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أنهم فعلوا ذلك في ركوعهم . والثاني : أنها نزلت فيهم وهم في ركوعهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r10.claim: A third interpretation takes bowing to mean voluntary prayer: they perform obligatory prayer and give alms while engaged in supererogatory prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p47#2/r10.anchor: والثالث : أنه أراد بالركوع التنفل , وبإقامة الصلاة الفرض من قولهم فلان يركع إذا انتفل بالصلاة .

MUQATIL:5:54-55/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r8.claim: At the first prayer, ʿAbd Allah b. Salam and his companions told the Prophet that the Jews had become hostile and stopped speaking or associating with them; their homes were among the Jews, and they found company only at the mosque.
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r8.anchor: قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم عند صلاة الأولى: إن اليهود أظهروا لنا العداوة من أجل الإسلام

MUQATIL:5:54-55/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r9.claim: After the Prophet recited the verse, Ibn Salam's group accepted God, the Messenger, and the believers as their allies; people then began praying voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayer at the first prayer.
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r9.anchor: فقرأها النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا: قد رضينا بالله ورسوله وبالمؤمنين أولياء

MUQATIL:5:54-55/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r10.claim: A beggar said ʿAli b. Abi Talib gave him his ring while bowing; the Prophet praised God for granting ʿAli this honor.
MUQATIL:5:54-55/r10.anchor: قال: الرجل القائم أعطانى خاتمه، يعنى على بن أبى طالب، رضوان الله عليه

MUQATIL:5:55-57/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r1.claim: Muqatil says God revealed the believers' clause after the report of ʿAli giving his ring while bowing.
MUQATIL:5:55-57/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل: { والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون }

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r1.claim: After forbidding alliance with those who must be opposed, the passage names those whose alliance is loved.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r1.anchor: عقب النهى عن موالاة من تجب معاداتهم ذكر من تحب موالاتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r2.claim: The singular «walī» despite a plural list makes God’s authority foundational and the others’ derivative; a plural would lose that hierarchy.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r2.anchor: الولاية لله أصل ولغيره تبع ولو قيل إنما أولياؤكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r3.claim: The phrase may be appositional to «those who believe», predicate of an implicit «they are», or an accusative of praise.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r3.anchor: الرفع على البدل من الذين آمنوا أو على هم الذين أو النصب على المدح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r4.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they give alms while bowing in prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r4.anchor: والواو فى ﴿ وهم راكعون ﴾ للحال أى يؤتونها فى حال ركوعهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.claim: It is said the verse came down about ʿAlī when a petitioner asked him as he bowed and he dropped his ring with little movement.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.anchor: قيل أنها نزلت فى على رضى الله عنه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع فى صلاته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.claim: The verse uses the plural although the reported occasion involved one person, encouraging others to imitate him and attain like reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.anchor: وورد بلفظ الجمع و إن كلان السبب فيه واحدا ترغيبا للناس فى مثل فعله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.claim: The verse shows charity during prayer is permissible and a small action does not invalidate prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.anchor: والآية تدل على جواز الصدقة فى الصلاة وعلى أن الفعل القليل لا يفسد الصلاة

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r1.claim: A Persian couplet before the explanation advises accepting what has been given and laying aside a frown, since neither party was granted choice.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r1.anchor: رضا بداده بده وزجبين كره بكشاي كه بر من وتوردر اختيار نكشادست

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r2.claim: The author prays to be among those granted divine care, special enabling, and guidance.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r2.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا ممن سبقت له العناية وتقدم في حقه التوفيق الخاص والهداية

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r3.claim: Do not take Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another, while your allies are God, His Messenger, and the believers, so grant loyalty to them alone.
