BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r3.anchor: أي لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء لأن بعضهم أولياء بعض وليسوا بأوليائكم إنما أولياؤكم الله ورسوله والمؤمنون

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r4.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author says loyalty to God means opposing everything besides Him, as Abraham says they are enemies except the Lord of the worlds.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r4.anchor: فموالاة الله في معاداة ما سوى الله كما قال الخليل عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r5.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author explains that loyalty to the Messenger requires opposing the self and resisting desire; a cited saying says desire must follow what the Prophet brought.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r5.anchor: وموالاة الرسول في معاداة النفس ومخالفة الهوى

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r6.claim: The author cites a Prophetic saying that faith is incomplete until the Messenger is more beloved than a person's self, wealth, children, and all people.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r6.anchor: لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحب إليه من نفسه وماله وولده والناس أجمعين

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r7.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author says loyalty to believers means fraternity in religion; the Qur'an calls believers brothers and a Prophetic saying enjoins loving for one's brother what one loves for oneself.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r7.anchor: وموالاة المؤمنين في مؤاخاتهم في الدين

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r8.claim: The phrase alladhina is appositional to alladhina amanu.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r8.anchor: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين} بدل من الذين آمنوا {وهم راكعون} حال من فاعل الفعلين

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r9.claim: The clause wa-hum raki'un is circumstantial for the agents of both verbs, and ruku is explained as humility and lowliness.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r9.anchor: {وهم راكعون} حال من فاعل الفعلين أي يعملون ما ذكر من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وهم خاشعون ومتواضعون

BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r10.claim: The purpose is to distinguish sincere believers from hypocrites: sincerity appears through regular prayer and almsgiving in a state of humble submission.
BURSEVI:v2p326#4/r10.anchor: والمقصود تمييز المؤمن المخلص ممن يدعي الإيمان ويكون منافقا لأن الإخلاص إنما يعرف بكونه مواظبا على الصلاة والزكاة في حال الركوع أي في حال الخشوع والإخبات

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r1.claim: Jabir reports that Abdullah b. Salam said Qurayza and Nadir had shunned his people and barred their company; distant homes kept them from joining the Prophet's companions, so this verse came down and they accepted God, His Messenger, and believers as allies.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r1.anchor: قال جابر بن عبد الله قال عبد الله بن سلام للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن قومنا من قريظة والنضير قد هجرونا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r2.claim: The relative phrase is general and means all believers.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r3.claim: Asked whether the believers meant Ali, Abu Ja'far answered that Ali is one of the believers, so the phrase concerns all believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r3.anchor: وقد سئل أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنهم عن معنى

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the general reading clear because al-ladhina is plural and denotes a group.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا قول بين لأن «الذين» لجماعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r5.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r6.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned Ali; Mujahid and al-Suddi also held this view because of the prayer, almsgiving, and bowing description.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه. وقال في رواية أخرى: نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وقاله مجاهد والسدي،

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r7.claim: A petitioner asked for help in the Prophet's mosque; Ali, praying in bowing with a ring on his right hand, gestured and the petitioner took it.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r7.anchor: أن سائلا سأل في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يعطه أحد شيئا، وكان علي في الصلاة في الركوع

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r8.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r8.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari infers that small action does not invalidate prayer: Ali gave the petitioner his ring while bowing and his prayer remained valid.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r8.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: وهذا يدل على أن العمل القليل لا يبطل الصلاة فإن التصدق بالخاتم في الركوع

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.claim: The ring gift shows voluntary alms can be called zakat; 30:39 includes obligatory and voluntary giving, as do sadaqa and salat.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.anchor: وقوله: { ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون } يدل على أن صدقة التطوع تسمى زكاة فإن عليا تصدق بخاتمه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r10.claim: Al-Qurtubi says it is strained to read zakat here as the ring gift: zakat has its specific obligatory sense, explained earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r10.anchor: وحمل لفظ الزكاة على التصدق بالخاتم فيه بعد لأن الزكاة لا تأتي إلا بلفظها المختص بها

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r11.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at proper times with all requirements; the intended prayer is obligatory prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r11.anchor: ومعنى يقيمون الصلاة يأتون بها في أوقاتها بجميع حقوقها، والمراد صلاة الفرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r12.claim: One explanation takes 'while bowing' as supererogatory prayer; another singles out bowing as an honorific mention.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r12.anchor: ثم قال: «وهم راكعون» أي النفل. وقيل: أفرد الركوع بالذكر تشريفا.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r13.claim: A further explanation says believers at revelation were divided between people completing prayer and people bowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r13.anchor: وقيل: المؤمنون وقت نزول الآية كانوا بين متم للصلاة وبين راكع.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r14.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r14.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad says the verse's praise establishes that slight action during prayer is permissible, and reports Ali gave a petitioner something while praying.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r14.anchor: وقال ابن خويزمنداد قوله تعالى: { ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون } تضمنت جواز العمل اليسير في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r15.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r15.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad allows that Ali's prayer may have been voluntary, since giving during an obligatory prayer is disliked.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r15.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون هذه صلاة تطوع، وذلك أنه مكروه في الفرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r16.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r16.claim: Alternatively, praise describes belief in the obligations of prayer and zakat, expressed as prayer and bowing without requiring a person to be praying then.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r16.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المدح متوجها على اجتماع حالتين كأنه وصف من يعتقد وجوب الصلاة والزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r1.claim: After forbidding alliance with disbelievers, God commands allegiance to those who deserve it.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r1.anchor: لما نهى في الآيات المتقدمة عن موالاة الكفار أمر في هذه الآية بموالاة من يجب موالاته

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r2.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r2.claim: After ʿUbādah renounced his pact with Qurayẓa and Naḍīr and declared allegiance to God and His Messenger, the verse was revealed in accord with him.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r2.anchor: عبادة بن الصامت لما تبرأ من اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r3.speaker: عبدالله بن سلام
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r3.claim: Ibn Salām said his people ostracized him and distance prevented him from joining the Prophet’s companions; the verse came, and they accepted God, the Messenger, and believers as allies.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r3.anchor: وروي أيضا أن عبدالله بن سلام قال : يا رسول الله إن قومنا قد هجرونا

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r4.claim: On the general reading, every believer is an ally of every other believer, as 9:71 also states.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r4.anchor: فعلى هذا : الآية عامة في حق كل المؤمنين ، فكل من كان مؤمنا فهو ولي كل المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r5.claim: The prayer and almsgiving description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocrites who claim faith but neglect prayer and are miserly; the cited descriptions are 9:54, 4:142, and 33:19.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r5.anchor: والمراد بذكر هذه الصفلات تمييز عن المنافقين

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r6.claim: Abū Muslim takes rukūʿ as submission: they pray and give alms while obedient and humble toward all God’s commands and prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من الركوع الخضوع

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r7.claim: Another view reads rukūʿ as prayer bowing, singled out to honor it, as in the command to bow with those who bow (2:43).
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r7.anchor: وخص الركوع بالذكر تشريفا له كما في قوله { واركعوا مع الراكعين }

RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r8.claim: Some say the companions were at different stages when it was revealed: some had finished prayer, some gave to a poor person, and some were still bowing, so all states are mentioned.
RAZI-FULL:v12p22#2/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن أصحابه كانوا عند نزول هذه الآية مختلفون

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r1.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r1.claim: ʿIkrimah reports that the verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r1.anchor: روى عكرمة أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r2.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r3.speaker: عبدالله بن سلام
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r3.claim: Ibn Salām says he saw ʿAlī give his ring to a needy person while bowing, and concluded that they should ally with him.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r3.anchor: روي أن عبدالله بن سلام قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية قلت يا رسول أنا رأيت عليا تصدق بخاتمه

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r4.claim: Abū Dharr recounts a petitioner receiving no alms, then ʿAlī signaling him to take his ring while bowing; the Prophet prayed for ʿAlī as his minister, and Gabriel brought the verse. No grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه أنه قال : صليت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما صلاة الظهر ، فسأل سائل

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r5.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r5.claim: The Shīʿa argue that the verse proves ʿAlī is the imam after the Prophet, reasoning that it identifies an imam and then identifying him as ʿAlī.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r5.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r6.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r6.claim: They argue that wali can mean both helper or beloved and one with authority; since the meanings can coexist, the righteous believers named here govern the community. They cite the guardian in a marriage report as usage evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r6.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r7.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r7.claim: Their second argument says innamā excludes a general meaning of support, leaving authority as the only other sense of wali; thus the described believers have authority over the whole community.
RAZI-FULL:v12p23/r7.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r1.speaker: القوم
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r1.claim: They infer ʿAlī specifically: all who take the verse to establish a particular imam identify him as ʿAlī; they reject Abū Bakr because that would imply his imamate, which they say the community does not accept from this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r1.anchor: وهذا حاصل استدلال القوم بهذه الآية على إمامة علي عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r2.speaker: القوم
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r2.claim: They say the bowing clause cannot coordinate with the prior description because prayer already includes bowing; it must be circumstantial, making giving alms while bowing specific to ʿAlī and proving his imamate.
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r2.anchor: وهذا حاصل استدلال القوم بهذه الآية على إمامة علي عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r3.claim: Rāzī rejects combining wali’s shared meanings of helper and authority: legal theory does not allow a homonym to bear both meanings at once.
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r3.anchor: أما حمل لفظ الولي على الناصر وعلى المتصرف معا فغير جائز ، لما ثبت في أصول الفقه أنه لا يجوز حمل اللفظ المشترك على مفهومية معا

RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r4.claim: The surrounding bans on taking Jews and Christians as allies in 5:51 and 5:57 show that wali here means helper and beloved; an imamate reading would interrupt a continuous argument.
RAZI-FULL:v12p24/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن الولاية المأمور بها ههنا هي المنهي عنها فيما قبل ، ولما كانت الولاية المنهي عنها فيما قبل هي الولاية بمعنى النصرة

RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r1.claim: Authority over the community did not belong to ʿAlī during the Prophet’s life, whereas love and support already did; the paired prohibition and command must apply at the same time.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r1.anchor: لأن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه ما كان نافذ التصرف حال حياة الرسول ، والآية تقتضي كون هؤلاء المؤمنون موصوفين بالولاية في الحال

RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r2.claim: The description uses plural forms repeatedly in seven places; applying them to one person is possible only figuratively, while the literal reading is a group.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر المؤمنين الموصوفين في هذه الآية بصيغة الجمع في سبعة مواضع

RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r3.claim: Rāzī says 5:54 strongly supports Abū Bakr’s imamate; reading 5:55 as ʿAlī’s immediate imamate would make the verses contradictory, so it cannot prove that succession.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r3.anchor: من أقوى الدلائل على صحة إمامة أبي بكر

RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r4.claim: ʿAlī knew Qurʾānic interpretation yet, when arguing at the council, cited the Ghadīr report, mutual invocation, and his merits but never this verse; Rāzī treats that silence as defeating the Shīʿī proof.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25/r4.anchor: وليس للقوم أن يقولوا : إنه تركه للتقية

RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r1.claim: Even if the verse implies ʿAlī’s imamate, it gives no date; Rāzī accepts an imamate after Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, since ʿAlī lacked authority during the Prophet’s life.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r1.anchor: بعد أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان ، إذ ليس في الآية ما يدل على تعيين الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that only two community positions are possible: the non-immediate reading is a third possibility, and the objection could naturally arise alongside the original proof.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r2.anchor: من الظاهر أنه منذ استدل مستدل بهذه الآية على إمامة علي

RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r3.claim: The community already knew God and His Messenger had authority; the verse reassures them that divine support leaves no need for alliance with unbelievers, so wali means supporter and beloved, not both homonymous senses.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r3.anchor: وإنما ذكر الله تعالى هذا الكلام تطييبا لقول المؤمنين وتعريفا لهم بأنه لا حاجة بهم إلى اتخاذ الأحباب والأنصار من الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r4.claim: Because wali occurs once, Rāzī says it cannot mean support and authority simultaneously under the rule against combining a homonym’s meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v12p25#2/r4.anchor: ولا شك أن لفظ الولي مذكور مرة واحدة ، فلما أريد به ههنا معنى النصرة امتنع أن يراد به معنى التصرف

RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r1.claim: Reading wali as love and support matches 5:54: its love and support descriptions are reaffirmed here, while its striving description parallels prayer and almsgiving in 5:55.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r1.anchor: على معنى المحبة والنصرة كان قوله { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله } يفيد فائدة قوله { يحبهم ويحبونه

RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r2.claim: Rāzī denies that innamā always restricts meaning, citing 10:24 and 47:36, where worldly life is called a likeness or play and diversion without excluding other descriptions.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r2.anchor: ولا نسلم أن كلمة { إنما } للحصر ، والدليل عليه قوله { إنما مثل الحيواة الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r3.claim: The verse can address one group as those under protection and name another as allies; support by the latter for the former need not be universal or self-support.

RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r4.claim: Thus restricting the specified allies does not rule out support as the meaning of wali; Rāzī calls this a subtle answer requiring reflection.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26/r4.anchor: فثبت أن نصرة أحد قسمي الأمة غير ثابتة لكل الأمة ، بل مخصوصة بالقسم الثاني من الأمة ، فلم يلزم من كون الولاية المذكورة في هذه الآية خاصة

RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r1.claim: Rāzī denies that the verse is specifically about ʿAlī: most commentators apply it to the whole community and its instruction to take Muslim allies; some say it concerns Abū Bakr.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r1.anchor: فقد بينا أن أكثر المفسرين زعموا أنه في حق الأمة ، والمراد أن الله تعالى أمر المسلم

RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r2.claim: Zakah ordinarily means obligatory alms (2:43); paying it late while bowing would delay a duty beyond its first time, sinful according to most scholars, so Rāzī rejects this attribution to ʿAlī and a voluntary-charity reading.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r2.anchor: أن الزكاة اسم للواجب لا للمندوب بدليل قوله تعالى { وإذ أخذنا }

RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r3.claim: Rāzī argues that ʿAlī should be absorbed in remembering God during prayer and unable to attend to another’s speech, invoking 3:191.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r3.anchor: أن اللائق بعلي عليه السلام أن يكون مستغرق القلب بذكر الله حال ما يكون في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r4.claim: Rāzī says ʿAlī had no wealth subject to obligatory zakah: the Shīʿī account that three loaves brought the praise of Sūrat al-Insān (76:1) implies poverty, so the ring gift cannot be the zakah meant here.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r4.anchor: فإنهم يقولون : إنه لما أعطى ثلاثة أقراص نزل فيه سورة { أهل * أتى }

RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r5.claim: Even granting that the verse refers to ʿAlī, the argument proves imamate only if wali means authority rather than support or love, which Rāzī has already rejected.
RAZI-FULL:v12p26#2/r5.anchor: هب أن المراد بهذه الآية هو علي بن أبي طالب لكنه لم يتم الاستدلال بالآية إلا إذا تم أن المراد بالولي هو المتصرف لا الناصر والمحب

RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r1.speaker: القائلون
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r1.claim: Those who take the verse to mean giving alms while bowing infer that a small action, such as handing charity to a petitioner during prayer, does not invalidate prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r1.anchor: الذين يقولون : المراد من قوله { ويؤتون الزكواة وهم راكعون } هو أنهم يؤتون الزكاة حال كونهم راكعين احتجوا بالآية على أن العمل القليل لا يقطع الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r2.claim: The singular wali makes God the primary source of allegiance, with the Messenger and believers included derivatively; a plural ‘allies’ would lose this primary-and-subordinate structure.
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r2.anchor: أصل الكلام إنما وليكم الله ، فجعلت الولاية لله على طريق الأصالة ، ثم نظم في سلك إثباتها له إثباتها لرسول الله والمؤمنين على سبيل التبع

RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r3.speaker: عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r3.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has mawlākum, ‘your protector/master,’ in place of waliyyukum.
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : إنما مولاكم الله

RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r4.claim: The phrase is parsed as nominative apposition to the preceding ‘those’ (as transmitted in the text), or as the predicate ‘they are those who pray,’ or as accusative for praise.
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r4.anchor: الجواب : الرفع على البدل من { الذين كفروا } أو يقال : هم الذين يقيمون ، أو النصب على المدح

RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r5.claim: The description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocritical claimants: sincere devotion is known through regular prayer, including bowing understood as humility and submission to God.
RAZI-FULL:v12p27/r5.anchor: والغرض من ذكره تمييز المؤمن المخلص عمن يدعي الإيمان ويكون منافقا ، لأن ذلك الإخلاص إنما يعرف بكونه مواظبا على الصلاة في حال الركوع
